children.title: Nested Activation Levels
children.top_down_role: Ordered activation regimes whose feasible regions form a nested structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integrality of the Nested-Indicator Chain Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal linear relaxation of a chain of prerequisite activation indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polytope \[Q_L=\{z\in\mathbb R^L:1\ge z_1\ge z_2\ge\cdots\ge z_L\ge0\}\] has exactly the \(L+1\) vertices \((0,\ldots,0),(1,0,\ldots,0),\ldots,(1,\ldots,1)\). Hence every vertex of \(Q_L\) is binary, and the monotone chain inequalities describe the convex hull of all feasible nested binary activation patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous monotone-chain relaxation is integral: its vertices are exactly the binary prefix-activation patterns.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is a positive integer.
The hierarchy is a single chain rather than a branching or conflicting prerequisite system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_L=\operatorname{conv}\{(\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{k},0,\ldots,0):k=0,\ldots,L\}.

notation.meaning: Deepest active level, with \(k=0\) denoting complete inactivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrality of the Nested-Indicator Chain Polytope

assumptions_latex: Indicators \(z_1,\ldots,z_L\) correspond to successively deeper activation levels.
A deeper level may operate only when every preceding level operates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nested activation is characterized by \(1\ge z_1\ge z_2\ge\cdots\ge z_L\ge0\) with binary \(z_r\).

notation.meaning: indicator for activation through level r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monotone binary indicators encode prerequisite activation along a chain
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chain-ordered binary activation hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z_r\in\{0,1\}\), nested activation levels satisfy \[z_{r+1}\le z_r\qquad(r=1,\ldots,L-1).\] Equivalently, \(1\ge z_1\ge z_2\ge\cdots\ge z_L\ge0\). Therefore activation of level \(r+1\) implies activation of every ancestor level, while deactivation of level \(r\) forces all deeper levels to be inactive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary indicators decrease along the hierarchy, so a deeper level can activate only after all of its ancestors activate.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Activation Levels

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotone binary-chain condition exactly expresses nested activation along a hierarchy and the condition kind is appropriate, but the record lacks a cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Shared-Indicator Coupling
children.top_down_role: Cross-activity dependence induced by a common activation indicator.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Indicator Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal coupling of several convex groups controlled by one binary indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_g\subset\mathbb R^{n_g}\) be nonempty compact convex sets for \(g=1,\ldots,m\). The closed convex hull of the shared-activation set \[S=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,1):x^g\in C_g\text{ for every }g\}\] is \[\operatorname{conv}(S)=\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ x^g\in zC_g\text{ for every }g\}.\] Thus every group must use the same relaxed indicator \(z\); replacing it by independently relaxed copies loses the shared coupling unless equality of those copies is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For compact convex groups sharing one indicator, the ideal relaxation scales every group by the same indicator. Independent indicator copies must be equated to retain this coupling.
assumptions_latex: \(C_g\subset\mathbb R^{n_g}\) is nonempty, compact, and convex for every \(g\).
The inactive state fixes every block \(x^g\) to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(S)=\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ x^g\in zC_g\ \forall g\}\).

notation.meaning: scaled set {z u: u in C_g}

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the shared-indicator leaf and the compact-convex hull formula is plausible, but no cited source or inspectable locator supports the ideal-hull and indicator-copy claims.

children.title: Activation-Hierarchy Failures
children.top_down_role: Invalid or weak representations caused by incompatible group or level relationships.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General ancestor-closure failure caused by omitting parent-child activation implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a directed activation hierarchy, where \((p,c)\in E\) means that child activation requires parent activation. For binary variables \(y_v\), the inequalities \[y_c\le y_p\qquad((p,c)\in E)\] enforce that every active node has all ancestors active. If an edge implication is neither imposed nor implied by the remaining constraints, the assignment \(y_c=1\), \(y_p=0\) is an admissible hierarchy violation, possibly together with a positive child-controlled activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hierarchy links make active sets ancestor-closed; omitting a nonredundant child-to-parent link permits an active child with an inactive parent.
assumptions_latex: \(y_v\in\{0,1\}\) for every hierarchy node.
Each directed edge \((p,c)\) represents the intended implication \(y_c=1\Rightarrow y_p=1\).
The omitted edge implication is not implied by other constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{v:y_v=1\}\text{ is ancestor-closed under all edge inequalities, while omission of a nonimplied edge permits }y_c=1,\ y_p=0.

notation.meaning: Activation indicator for hierarchy node v.

knowledge_statements.title: Omitted Hierarchy-Edge Failure
Activation-Hierarchy Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by omitting logical inequalities between parent and child activations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y,z\in\{0,1\}\) denote parent and child activations, with the intended implication \(z=1\Rightarrow y=1\), and let \(0\le x\le z\) be a child variable. If the formulation contains only \(0\le x\le z\), \(0\le y,z\le1\), then \((x,y,z)=(1,0,1)\) is feasible although it violates the hierarchy. Consequently, even ideal formulations for the individual on-off blocks do not recover hierarchical validity: the coupling inequality \(z\le y\), or an equivalent joint formulation, is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ideal formulations for separate activation blocks do not enforce ancestry. Without the child-to-parent inequality, a child can be active while its parent is inactive.
assumptions_latex: The intended hierarchy requires child activation to imply parent activation.
No constraint equivalent to \(z\le y\) is present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((1,0,1)\) is a feasible hierarchy-violating point, so separate on-off constraints are insufficient.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the displayed point correctly demonstrates the omitted implication. A specific source and locator are nevertheless required for candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Perspective Reformulation Principle
children.top_down_role: Perspective-based convexification of activated convex epigraphs and feasible regions.

children.title: Closed-Perspective Geometry
children.top_down_role: Closure behavior at the inactive boundary of perspective constructions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel Representation of the Closed Perspective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual affine-minorant representation of closed-perspective geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex function \(f\) and \(z\ge0\), \[f^{\pi}(x,z)=\sup_{s\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\{s^{\mathsf T}x-zf^*(s)\}.\] Hence \(f^{\pi}(x,0)=\sup_{s\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}s^{\mathsf T}x=f^{\infty}(x)\), and \[\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\{(x,z,t):z\ge0,\ t\ge s^{\mathsf T}x-zf^*(s)\ \forall s\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective is the supremum of homogenized Fenchel minorants, whose zero-activation value is the recession function.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^{\pi}(x,z)=\sup_{s\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\bigl(s^{\mathsf T}x-zf^*(s)\bigr)\quad(z\ge0).
knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel Representation of the Closed Perspective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric conic representation of the closed perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex function \(f\), \[\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{(u,1,r):(u,r)\in\operatorname{epi}f\}.\] Positive-activation slices are scaled copies of \(\operatorname{epi}f\), and closure supplies the recession epigraph at zero activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective epigraph is the closed homogenization cone of the original epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\{(u,1,r):(u,r)\in\operatorname{epi}f\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Homogenized Epigraph-Cone Representation
Closed-Perspective Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-semicontinuous closure of a convex perspective at zero activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), its closed perspective is \[f^{\pi}(x,z)=\begin{cases}z f(x/z),&z>0,\\ f^{\infty}(x),&z=0,\\ +\infty,&z<0,\end{cases}\] where \(f^{\infty}\) is the recession function of \(f\). The function \(f^{\pi}\) is proper, closed, convex, and positively homogeneous. Its epigraph is the closure of the epigraph obtained from \(z f(x/z)\) on \(z>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective extends the ordinary perspective to zero activation using the recession function, producing a closed convex, positively homogeneous function.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^{\pi}\) is the lower-semicontinuous closure of the perspective on \(z>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches closed-perspective geometry and consistently uses the recession function at zero, but its closure, convexity, homogeneity, and epigraph claims lack an authoritative convex-analysis citation with a locator.

children.title: Perspective Epigraph Formulations
children.top_down_role: Lifted representations for activated convex objective or epigraph terms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact closed hull of an on-off convex epigraph without compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and define \[S=\{(0,0,t):t\ge0\}\cup\{(x,1,t):t\ge F(x)\}.\] Then \[\operatorname{clconv}S=\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge F^{\pi}(x,z)\}.\] At \(z=0\), the slice is \(t\ge F^{\infty}(x)\). Nonzero inactive arguments therefore occur exactly in directions where the recession value is finite; a compact effective domain reduces this slice to \(x=0,\ t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective epigraph is the exact closed hull of an on-off convex epigraph, with the recession epigraph forming its inactive boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{clconv}S=\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge F^{\pi}(x,z)\}.

notation.meaning: union of inactive and active epigraph branches
recession function determining the inactive boundary

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Aware Perspective Epigraph Hull
Perspective Epigraph Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal lifted epigraph for a compact convex on-off domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be closed and convex, and define \(F=f+\delta_C\). For \[S=\{(0,0,t):t\ge0\}\cup\{(x,1,t):x\in C,\ t\ge f(x)\},\] the closed convex hull is \[\operatorname{clconv}(S)=\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge F^{\pi}(x,z)\}.\] Compactness ensures that the zero-activation slice of this perspective epigraph has \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective epigraph gives the ideal continuous relaxation of a compact convex epigraph that is either inactive at zero or fully active.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}(S)=\{(x,z,t):0\le z\le1,\ t\ge F^{\pi}(x,z)\}\).

notation.meaning: closed perspective of the extended-valued function F

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and compact-domain perspective construction fit the epigraph-formulation leaf. The exact closed-convex-hull equality and its zero-activation interpretation require an authoritative theorem or section locator.

children.title: Perspective Constraint Formulations
children.top_down_role: Perspective strengthening for activated convex feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex hull of an activated convex feasible region, including its zero-activation recession slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{x:g(x)\le0\}\) be nonempty and closed convex, where \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex, and assume \(\operatorname{rec}C=\{d:g^{\infty}(d)\le0\}\). For \(S=\{(0,0)\}\cup(C\times\{1\})\), \[\operatorname{clconv}S=\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ g^{\pi}(x,z)\le0\}.\] Its zero-activation slice is \(\{(d,0):d\in\operatorname{rec}C\}\). Consequently, adding \(x=0\) at \(z=0\) preserves this closed hull exactly when \(\operatorname{rec}C=\{0\}\), in particular when \(C\) is compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perspective hull of an unbounded activated convex region retains recession directions at zero activation; forcing the inactive vector to zero is exact only when no nonzero recession direction exists.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(C=\{x:g(x)\le0\}\) is nonempty and closed.
\(\operatorname{rec}C=\{d:g^{\infty}(d)\le0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{clconv}S=\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ g^{\pi}(x,z)\le0\}.

notation.meaning: recession cone of the active region

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Aware Activated-Constraint Hull
Perspective Constraint Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-perspective strengthening of an activated convex inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and suppose \(C=\{x:g(x)\le0\}\) is nonempty and compact. For the disjunction \[S=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,1):g(x)\le0\},\] its closed convex hull is represented by \[0\le z\le1,\qquad g^{\pi}(x,z)\le0.\] Equivalently, the positive-activation constraint is \(z g(x/z)\le0\); the closed-perspective value at \(z=0\) supplies the correct inactive boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An activated convex inequality is strengthened by applying its closed perspective. Under compactness, the resulting relaxation is the closed convex hull of the on-off set.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\{x:g(x)\le0\}\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}(S)=\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ g^{\pi}(x,z)\le0\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the activated-constraint leaf, and compactness plausibly removes nonzero recession directions at zero activation. The asserted exact hull equality has no supporting citation or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex hull of an activated power set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The set \(C\) and parameter conditions on \(a,b,l,u\) are inherited from the preceding setup; those unstated conditions must not be inferred from this extract.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the conditions of the preceding setup, the convex hull of the activated power set is described by the perspective power inequality, activation-scaled bounds on x, a relaxed activation variable between zero and one, and nonnegativity of x and y.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perspective extended formulation for a union of bounded convex sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull representation using disaggregated variables, simplex weights, and the source-defined perspective functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each $t\in T$, let $G^t:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{m_t}$ and let $K^t=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:G^t(x)\le 0\}$ be convex and bounded. Define $K=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{t\in T}K^t)$. Then $x\in K$ if and only if there exist $(x^t,\lambda_t)_{t\in T}$ such that $x=\sum_{t\in T}x^t$, $\sum_{t\in T}\lambda_t=1$, $\widetilde G^t(\lambda_t,x^t)\le0$, and $\lambda_t\ge0$ for all $t\in T$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of the union of the bounded convex sets is the projection of the stated disaggregated perspective system.

K^t=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:G^t(x)\le0\}\text{ is convex and bounded for every }t\in T
K=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{t\in T}K^t\right)

children.title: Multivariate Perspective Formulations
children.top_down_role: Perspective constructions involving jointly activated vectors or blocks.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent Activations Do Not Model Joint Activation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between one common block indicator and independently activated blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty active sets \(C_q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_q}\), the jointly activated set \[S_{\mathrm{joint}}=\{(0,\ldots,0,0)\}\cup\{(x_1,\ldots,x_p,1):x_q\in C_q\ \forall q\}\] is not represented by replacing the common indicator with independent indicators \(z_q\). The independent model admits mixed activation states absent from \(S_{\mathrm{joint}}\). Separate block perspectives represent joint activation only when constraints enforce \(z_1=\cdots=z_p\), or equivalent coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different block indicators change joint activation into independent activation unless they are explicitly coupled to one common value.
assumptions_latex: The proposed separate-indicator model permits at least two indicators to differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_{\mathrm{independent}}=S_{\mathrm{joint}}\text{ requires }z_1=\cdots=z_p\text{ or equivalent coupling}.

notation.meaning: set activated by one common indicator

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Activations Do Not Model Joint Activation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block decomposition of a separable multivariate perspective under one common activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\) and \(f(x)=\sum_{q=1}^p f_q(x_q)\), where every \(f_q\) is proper, closed, and convex. For one common activation variable \(z\ge0\), \[f^{\pi}(x,z)=\sum_{q=1}^p f_q^{\pi}(x_q,z).\] The identity includes \(z=0\), where both sides equal the sum of the block recession functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-separable convex function decomposes into block perspectives when every block uses the same activation variable.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_q\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The coordinate blocks are disjoint and share one activation variable \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\sum_q f_q\right)^{\pi}(x,z)=\sum_qf_q^{\pi}(x_q,z)\quad(z\ge0).

notation.meaning: closed perspective of the q-th block function

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Activation Separability
Multivariate Perspective Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One indicator jointly activates an entire vector or block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex. Joint activation of \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) by \(z\) uses the vector perspective epigraph \[0\le z\le1,\qquad t\ge f^{\pi}(x,z),\] where, for \(z>0\), \(f^{\pi}(x,z)=z f(x/z)\) and the division scales every coordinate of \(x\) by the same \(z\). At \(z=0\), the recession value \(f^{\infty}(x)\) gives the closed boundary; additional bounds \(x\in zC\) force \(x=0\) when \(C\) is compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multivariate perspective scales a jointly activated vector by one common indicator, with the recession function defining the closed zero-activation boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
All coordinates or blocks of \(x\) share the same activation variable \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge f^{\pi}(x,z)\) is a closed convex joint-activation epigraph formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly describes common scaling of a vector and fits the multivariate-perspective leaf, but no authoritative source supports the closed-boundary and joint-activation claims.

children.title: Conic Perspective Families

children.title: Quadratic Perspective Formulations
children.top_down_role: Perspective strengthening for activated convex quadratic structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular Quadratic Perspective Does Not Enforce Inactivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp nullspace counterexample at zero activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\), \(x=(0,1)\), \(z=0\), and \(t=0\). Then \(tz=0=x^{\mathsf T}Qx\), so the closed quadratic-perspective inequality is satisfied although \(x\ne0\). Thus a singular quadratic perspective alone does not impose the intended inactive fixing \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero nullspace vector satisfies a singular quadratic perspective at zero activation, so separate activation bounds may be indispensable.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(tz\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) holds while \(z=0\) and \(x\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Quadratic Perspective Does Not Enforce Inactivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed perspectives of positive-semidefinite quadratic forms and affine least-squares terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succeq0\). The closed perspective epigraph of \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) is \[z\ge0,\quad t\ge0,\quad tz\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx.\] At \(z=0\), it permits exactly the directions satisfying \(Q^{1/2}x=0\). More generally, for \(q(y)=\|Ay-b\|_2^2\), its closed perspective epigraph is \[z\ge0,\quad t\ge0,\quad tz\ge\|Ax-bz\|_2^2.\] At \(z=0\), this permits exactly \(x\in\ker A\). Separate activation bounds are therefore required when the intended inactive state is \(x=0\) and the quadratic map has a nontrivial nullspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic perspectives become product inequalities; affine residuals homogenize as Ax−bz, and nullspace directions survive at zero activation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.
\(A\) and \(b\) have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed product inequalities are the exact closed epigraphs of the homogeneous quadratic and affine least-squares perspectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous and Shifted Quadratic Perspectives
Quadratic Perspective Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective epigraph of a positive-semidefinite quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succeq0\). The closed perspective epigraph of \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) is \[\{(x,z,t):z\ge0,\ t\ge0,\ tz\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx\}.\] For \(z>0\), this is exactly \(t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx/z\). At \(z=0\), it requires \(Q^{1/2}x=0\); if the intended inactive state is \(x=0\) and \(Q\) is singular, separate activation bounds such as \(x\in zC\) are also required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic perspective is represented by a product inequality. At zero activation it eliminates directions seen by the quadratic, with bounds needed for nullspace directions.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.
\(z\) and \(t\) are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge q^{\pi}(x,z)\) is equivalent to \(tz\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx\), \(z,t\ge0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic perspective formula and singular-nullspace qualification are mathematically plausible and appropriate for this representation leaf. An authoritative source with a precise locator is missing.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of S is exactly described by the quadratic perspective inequality, scaled bounds, activation bounds, and stated nonnegativity conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(S)=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{R}^3:yz\ge x^2,\ lz\le x\le uz,\ 0\le z\le1,\ x\ge0,\ y\ge0\}

children.title: Second-Order-Cone Perspectives
children.top_down_role: Perspective formulations represented through ordinary or rotated second-order cones.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary behavior of an SOC perspective when cone membership alone does not enforce the intended inactive point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the homogeneous second-order-cone constraint \[\|Ax+bz\|_2\le c^{\mathsf T}x+dz,\qquad z\ge0,\] the zero-activation slice is \[\|Ax\|_2\le c^{\mathsf T}x.\] Consequently, this cone constraint alone fixes \(x=0\) at \(z=0\) if and only if \(K_0=\{x:\|Ax\|_2\le c^{\mathsf T}x\}=\{0\}\). If \(K_0\ne\{0\}\), the formulation contains nonzero recession directions at zero activation, and a model requiring a singleton inactive state needs additional valid linking restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero activation, an SOC perspective retains a recession slice and enforces the inactive point by itself only when that slice is trivial.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(d\in\mathbb R\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(z\ge0\).
The intended inactive branch requires \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x=0\text{ follows from the SOC constraint at }z=0\iff K_0=\{0\}.

notation.meaning: zero-activation recession slice of the homogeneous SOC constraint

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Activation Recession Slice
Second-Order-Cone Perspectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone-native homogenization of activated second-order-cone inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex inequality \(\|Ax+b\|_2\le c^{\mathsf T}x+d\). Its closed homogeneous perspective with activation variable \(z\ge0\) is \[\|Ax+bz\|_2\le c^{\mathsf T}x+dz.\] Hence the perspective is represented by membership \((c^{\mathsf T}x+dz,Ax+bz)\in\mathcal Q\) in the ordinary second-order cone. In particular, the quadratic perspective \(tz\ge\|Rx\|_2^2\), \(t,z\ge0\), is membership in a rotated second-order cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perspective homogenization preserves second-order-cone representability: constants are multiplied by the activation variable, and quadratic-over-linear terms use a rotated cone.
assumptions_latex: The original inequality has a valid second-order-cone representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((c^{\mathsf T}x+dz,Ax+bz)\in\mathcal Q\) represents the closed conic perspective.

notation.meaning: factor of a positive-semidefinite quadratic form

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conic representation fits the leaf, but no cited locator establishes the closed homogenization and rotated-cone claims. The dimensions and compatible domains of A, b, c, d, and x should also be made explicit when sourced.

children.title: Power-Cone Perspectives
children.top_down_role: Perspective representations using power-cone structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-cone formulation of scalar and weighted separable absolute-power perspectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p>1\), \(\alpha=1/p\), and \[\mathcal K_{\mathrm{pow}}^{\alpha}=\{(u,v,w):u,v\ge0,\ u^{\alpha}v^{1-\alpha}\ge|w|\}.\] The closed scalar perspective of \(|x|^p\) is represented by \[(t,z,x)\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{pow}}^{\alpha},\] equivalently \(tz^{p-1}\ge|x|^p\). More generally, for \(a_i>0\), the closed epigraph \[t\ge z\sum_{i=1}^m a_i|x_i/z|^p\] is represented by \[(s_i,z,x_i)\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{pow}}^{\alpha}\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad\sum_{i=1}^m a_i s_i\le t.\] At \(z=0\), these constraints force every \(x_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One power cone represents a scalar absolute-power perspective; a product of such cones and one linear aggregation represents a weighted separable sum.
assumptions_latex: \(p>1\) and \(\alpha=1/p\).
\(a_i>0\) for every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scalar and weighted separable \(p\)-power perspectives have the displayed exact closed power-cone representations.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar and Separable Power-Cone Perspectives
Power-Cone Perspectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-cone representation of scalar power perspectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(p>1\) and set \(\alpha=1/p\). The closed perspective epigraph of \(f(x)=|x|^p\) is \[t\ge0,\quad z\ge0,\quad t\ge z|x/z|^p\text{ for }z>0,\] with its closed value at \(z=0\). It has the power-cone representation \[(t,z,x)\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{pow}}^{\alpha},\qquad \mathcal K_{\mathrm{pow}}^{\alpha}=\{(u,v,w):u,v\ge0,\ u^{\alpha}v^{1-\alpha}\ge|w|\}.\] Indeed, membership is equivalent to \(t z^{p-1}\ge|x|^p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perspective of an absolute p-th power is exactly a power-cone constraint with exponent 1/p.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge z|x/z|^p\) is represented by \((t,z,x)\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{pow}}^{1/p}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exponent and coordinate convention are internally consistent: membership gives t z^{p-1} greater than or equal to |x|^p. The exact closed perspective representation still lacks an authoritative power-cone citation and locator.

children.title: Exponential-Cone Perspectives
children.top_down_role: Perspective representations for exponential and entropy-related convex terms.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed exponential-cone representations of exponential and relative-entropy perspectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\mathcal K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(a,b,c):b>0,\ b\exp(a/b)\le c\}.\] The closed exponential perspective satisfies \[t\ge z\exp(x/z)\quad(z>0),\qquad\text{with closure,}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(x,z,t)\in\mathcal K_{\exp}.\] Its zero-scale slice is \(z=0,\ x\le0,\ t\ge0\). The closed relative-entropy epigraph is \[t\ge x\log(x/y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(-t,x,y)\in\mathcal K_{\exp}.\] It has value zero when \(x=0,y\ge0\), and no finite epigraph value when \(x>0,y=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential cone exactly represents closed exponential perspectives and, after permuting coordinates, relative-entropy epigraphs with their correct boundary values.
assumptions_latex: The stated closed exponential-cone convention is used.
Perspective scales and relative-entropy arguments use their closed nonnegative domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,z,t)\in\mathcal K_{\exp}\) represents the closed exponential perspective, and \((-t,x,y)\in\mathcal K_{\exp}\) represents relative entropy.
knowledge_statements.title: Exponential and Relative-Entropy Perspective Representations
Exponential-Cone Perspectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential-cone representation of exponential perspective epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the closed exponential cone by \[\mathcal K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(x,z,t):z>0,\ z\exp(x/z)\le t\}.\] The closed perspective epigraph of \(f(x)=\exp(x)\) is therefore represented exactly by \[(x,z,t)\in\mathcal K_{\exp}.\] Its zero-scale boundary is \(z=0\), \(x\le0\), and \(t\ge0\). Thus exponential and related entropy perspectives can be modeled without dividing by a potentially zero activation variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Membership in the closed exponential cone exactly represents the exponential perspective and includes its correct zero-activation boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(z\) is a nonnegative perspective scale.
\(\mathcal K_{\exp}\) uses the stated closed-cone convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge z\exp(x/z)\) for \(z>0\), together with its closure, is equivalent to \((x,z,t)\in\mathcal K_{\exp}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cone convention, perspective formula, and stated zero-scale boundary are consistent and fit the leaf. No authoritative exponential-cone definition or section locator is supplied.

children.title: Perspective Realization Methods
children.top_down_role: Modeling and solver interfaces used to expose perspective strength without specifying full solution algorithms.

children.title: Explicit Nonlinear Perspective Models
children.top_down_role: Perspective formulations supplied directly to nonlinear optimization interfaces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epsilon Regularization Changes the Inactive Slice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete failure of replacing the activation denominator by a positive regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=x^2\), the closed perspective permits at \(z=0\) only \(x=0\) with \(t\ge0\). For any \(\varepsilon>0\), the regularized inequality \[t\ge\frac{x^2}{z+\varepsilon},\qquad z\ge0,\] admits every \((x,0,t)\) satisfying \(t\ge x^2/\varepsilon\), including points with \(x\ne0\). It therefore strictly enlarges the inactive slice and is not the exact perspective formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding epsilon to the denominator admits nonzero inactive arguments and changes the feasible set even for a quadratic.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{(x,z,t):z\ge0,\ t\ge x^2/(z+\varepsilon)\}\ne\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}.
knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon Regularization Changes the Inactive Slice

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Derivatives of a Smooth Positive Perspective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative formulas for direct nonlinear evaluation at positive activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be twice differentiable and convex on an open convex domain. For \(z>0\), set \(u=x/z\) and \(g(x,z)=zf(x/z)\). Then \[
abla_xg=
abla f(u),\qquad \partial_zg=f(u)-
abla f(u)^{\mathsf T}u,\] and \[
abla^2g(x,z)= rac1z egin{bmatrix}I\-u^{\mathsf T}\end{bmatrix}
abla^2f(u) egin{bmatrix}I&-u\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.\] Thus the positive-activation expression is jointly convex and admits exact first- and second-order oracle evaluations away from \(z=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At positive activation, a smooth perspective has explicit gradient and positive-semidefinite Hessian formulas suitable for nonlinear evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable and convex on an open convex domain.
\(z>0\) and \(x/z\) belongs to the domain of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla^2g(x,z)\succeq0\text{ and the displayed derivative formulas hold.}
knowledge_statements.title: Derivatives of a Smooth Positive Perspective
Explicit Nonlinear Perspective Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct extended-valued nonlinear encoding of a closed perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex function \(f\), an explicit nonlinear perspective model imposes \[t\ge\begin{cases}z f(x/z),&z>0,\\ f^{\infty}(x),&z=0,\end{cases}\qquad z\ge0.\] This is an exact closed convex formulation when the modeling interface honors the extended-valued boundary. Evaluating only \(z f(x/z)\) is undefined at \(z=0\); replacing \(z\) by \(z+\varepsilon\) generally changes the feasible set and is not the exact perspective formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct nonlinear model must implement both the positive-activation formula and the recession boundary. Epsilon regularization is generally inexact.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The nonlinear interface can represent the boundary or an equivalent domain restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge f^{\pi}(x,z)\), \(z\ge0\), is the exact explicit nonlinear perspective model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits explicit nonlinear realization and correctly distinguishes the recession boundary from epsilon regularization. The interface-dependent exactness and inexactness claims require a solver-modeling or convex-analysis source with a precise locator.

children.title: Explicit Conic Perspective Models
children.top_down_role: Perspective formulations supplied through cone-native representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone-native realization of the closed perspective of the exponential function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\le w\}.\] Then \[\operatorname{epi}(\exp)^{\pi}=K_{\exp}.\] Thus \((x,z,t)\in K_{\exp}\) represents \(t\ge z\exp(x/z)\) for \(z>0\) together with its lower-semicontinuous boundary at \(z=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed exponential cone is exactly the epigraph of the closed perspective of the exponential function.
assumptions_latex: \(K_{\exp}\) is taken with its closure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}(\exp)^{\pi}=K_{\exp}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exponential-Cone Perspective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone-native realization of the closed perspective of a positive-semidefinite quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=L^{\mathsf T}L\succeq0\) and define \(\mathcal Q_r=\{(a,b,w):a\ge0,\ b\ge0,\ 2ab\ge\|w\|_2^2\}\). Then the closed perspective epigraph of \(x\mapsto x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) is \[\{(x,z,t):(t,z,\sqrt2Lx)\in\mathcal Q_r\}.\] For \(z>0\) this is \(t\ge x^{\mathsf T}Qx/z\); at \(z=0\) it enforces \(Lx=0\), exactly matching the recession boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective of a positive-semidefinite quadratic form is represented by one rotated second-order-cone constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\).
\(Q=L^{\mathsf T}L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}(x\mapsto x^{\mathsf T}Qx)^{\pi}=\{(x,z,t):(t,z,\sqrt2Lx)\in\mathcal Q_r\}.

notation.meaning: factor of the positive-semidefinite matrix Q

knowledge_statements.title: Rotated-Cone Quadratic Perspective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-cone realization of the closed perspective of an absolute power.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p>1\), let \(\alpha=1/p\) and define \[K_{\alpha}=\{(u,v,w):u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ u^{\alpha}v^{1-\alpha}\ge|w|\}.\] Then \[(t,z,x)\in K_{1/p}\] is equivalent for \(z>0\) to \[t\ge \frac{|x|^p}{z^{p-1}},\] and its closed boundary at \(z=0\) forces \(x=0\). Hence it exactly represents the closed perspective epigraph of \(x\mapsto |x|^p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective of an absolute power is represented by a three-dimensional power-cone constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(K_{1/p}\) is the closed power cone under the stated convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}(x\mapsto|x|^p)^{\pi}=\{(x,z,t):(t,z,x)\in K_{1/p}\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Power-Cone Monomial Perspective
Explicit Conic Perspective Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenization of a cone representation to model its perspective natively.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the epigraph of a proper closed convex function has the conic representation \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):\exists y,\ Ax+bt+By+c\in K\},\] where \(K\) is a closed convex cone. Its homogeneous conic perspective formulation is \[z\ge0,\qquad \exists y:\ Ax+bt+By+cz\in K.\] Under the usual closedness condition for the projected homogeneous system, this set equals \(\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}\). Constants are scaled by \(z\), whereas variables already belonging to the homogeneous conic system are not divided by \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone-representable epigraph is perspectivized by homogenizing its affine conic system: multiply constant terms by the activation scale and retain cone membership.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
The stated epigraph representation is exact.
The projection of the homogenized conic system is closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\{(x,z,t):z\ge0,\ \exists y,\ Ax+bt+By+cz\in K\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The homogeneous conic representation fits the leaf, but the exact projected-epigraph equality and sufficient closedness condition need authoritative verification. The spaces and dimensions of the linear maps, vectors, and auxiliary variables should also be stated explicitly.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(f^{\pi}\) denote its closed perspective. For every \(\bar u\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(s\in\partial f(\bar u)\), each \((x,z,t)\in\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}\) satisfies \[t\ge s^{\mathsf T}x+\bigl(f(\bar u)-s^{\mathsf T}\bar u\bigr)z.\] Moreover, the complete cut family represents the epigraph as \[\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\left\{(x,z,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R:z\ge0,\ t\ge s^{\mathsf T}x+\bigl(f(\bar u)-s^{\mathsf T}\bar u\bigr)z\ \text{for all }\bar u\in\operatorname{dom}f,\ s\in\partial f(\bar u)\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective epigraph is represented by nonnegative activation together with all linear inequalities generated by subgradients of the active convex function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation over the full closed perspective epigraph, with subgradient specialization at positive activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((\hat x,\hat z,\hat t)\) with \(\hat z\ge0\), seek \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\) such that \[y^{\mathsf T}\hat x-\hat zf^*(y)>\hat t.\] Any such \(y\) returns the valid separating cut \[t\ge y^{\mathsf T}x-zf^*(y).\] The query belongs to \(\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}\) exactly when no such \(y\) exists. If \(\hat z>0\), \(\hat u=\hat x/\hat z\), and \(s\in\partial f(\hat u)\), choosing \(y=s\) makes the cut right-hand side at the query equal \(\hat zf(\hat u)\), yielding violation \(\hat zf(\hat u)-\hat t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A violated conjugate support separates any closed-perspective query; at positive activation, a subgradient at the normalized point gives the standard exact perspective tangent.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
A conjugate support oracle is available; for the positive-activation specialization, a subgradient at \(\hat x/\hat z\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y^{\mathsf T}\hat x-\hat zf^*(y)>\hat t\implies t\ge y^{\mathsf T}x-zf^*(y)\text{ is a valid violated perspective cut.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual parameterization of affine support inequalities for the closed perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, with Fenchel conjugate \(f^*\). For \(z\ge0\), \[f^{\pi}(x,z)=\sup_{y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\{y^{\mathsf T}x-zf^*(y)\}.\] Consequently, \[\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\{(x,z,t):z\ge0,\ t\ge y^{\mathsf T}x-zf^*(y)\ \forall y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\}.\] If \(y\in\partial f(\bar u)\), Fenchel equality gives \(-f^*(y)=f(\bar u)-y^{\mathsf T}\bar u\), recovering the subgradient form in the accepted seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perspective cuts are equivalently indexed by vectors in the conjugate domain; Fenchel equality recovers the usual subgradient cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^{\pi}(x,z)=\sup_{y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*}\bigl(y^{\mathsf T}x-zf^*(y)\bigr),\qquad z\ge0.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(f^{\pi}\) be its closed perspective. Define the unit-interval perspective epigraph by \[E=\left\{(x,z,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times[0,1]\times\mathbb R:t\ge f^{\pi}(x,z)\right\}.\] Choose a finite set \(J\) and pairs \((u_j,s_j)\) satisfying \(u_j\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(s_j\in\partial f(u_j)\). Its static polyhedral outer approximation is \[P_J=\left\{(x,z,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times[0,1]\times\mathbb R:t\ge s_j^{\mathsf T}x+\bigl(f(u_j)-s_j^{\mathsf T}u_j\bigr)z\quad(j\in J)\right\}.\] Then \(E\subseteq P_J\). If \(J\subseteq K\), then \(P_K\subseteq P_J\). Equality \(P_J=E\) holds whenever the selected affine minorants represent \(f^{\pi}\) exactly throughout \(\mathbb R^n\times[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite, preselected collection of perspective cuts gives a static polyhedral outer approximation on the unit activation interval, and adding cuts can only strengthen it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness Limit for Finite Static Supports
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness of finitely many preselected perspective supports on an active-variable region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_j(u)=s_j^{\mathsf T}u+f(u_j)-s_j^{\mathsf T}u_j\), where \(s_j\in\partial f(u_j)\), and let \(D\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\). On points with \(z>0\) and \(x/z\in D\), the static approximation is exact if and only if \[f(u)=\max_{j\in J}a_j(u)\qquad(u\in D).\] Consequently, no finite selected family is exact on \(D\) when \(f|_D\) is not representable as a finite maximum of affine functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite perspective supports are exact on a region exactly when their affine minorants reproduce the active convex function there.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Perspective Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural recognition and replacement of eligible on-off convex terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a model containing a binary variable \(z\), variables \(x\), and a convex epigraph constraint. Detect whether the model enforces \(x=0\) whenever \(z=0\) and whether the active constraint is \(t\ge f(x)\) when \(z=1\), with \(f\) proper, closed, and convex. Verify that no omitted constraint changes the inactive point or active domain. If all tests pass, replace the continuous relaxation by \(t\ge f^{\pi}(x,z)\), or generate valid perspective cuts; otherwise retain the original formulation and report the failed test. Output the transformed constraint and its detected activation set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A detector verifies convexity, the inactive point, active-domain equivalence, and coupling before introducing a perspective constraint or cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(z\in\{0,1\}\) is the candidate indicator.
The modeling system can inspect variable bounds, domains, and constraint incidence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A perspective reformulation is emitted only when the detected disjunction equals the modeled on-off set.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Active Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-perspective validity fails when the active epigraph is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Convexity of the active function is essential for direct perspective convexification. For example, let \(f(x)=-x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\). For \(z>0\), its homogeneous perspective is \(zf(x/z)=-x^2/z\), which is concave rather than convex in \((x,z)\). Consequently, the set \[\left\{(x,z,t):z>0,\ t\ge -x^2/z\right\}\] is nonconvex and cannot be used as a convex hull formulation of the associated on-off epigraph. A valid convex reformulation requires a separate convex envelope over a specified bounded domain or a genuinely nonconvex method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct perspective of a nonconvex active function need not be convex; a domain-specific convex envelope or nonconvex method is required.
assumptions_latex: The active function is \(f(x)=-x^2\).
The perspective is evaluated for \(z>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}(zf(x/z))\) is nonconvex, so direct convex-perspective reformulation is unavailable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-Envelope Perspective on a Compact Active Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convexification is recovered by convexifying the active extended-valued function before perspectivizing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and set \(g=\operatorname{cl\,conv}(f+\delta_D)\). For \[S=\{(0,0,t):t\ge0\}\cup\{(x,1,t):x\in D,\ t\ge f(x)\},\] one has \[\operatorname{cl\,conv}S=\operatorname{epi}g^{\pi}.\] Thus the direct perspective of nonconvex \(f\) is not the hull construction; the active epigraph must first be replaced by its closed convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact active domain, the exact closed on-off hull is the perspective of the closed convex envelope of the active extended-valued function.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is nonempty and compact.
\(f\) is proper and lower semicontinuous on \(D\).
The inactive epigraph is \(\{(0,0,t):t\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cl\,conv}S=\operatorname{epi}\bigl(\operatorname{cl\,conv}(f+\delta_D)\bigr)^{\pi}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex. Consider the inactive branch \(z=0\), \(x=0\), and \(t\ge\alpha\), where \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), and the active branch \(z=1\) and \(t\ge f(x)\). For \(0<z\le1\), their convexification satisfies \[t\ge(1-z)\alpha+zf(x/z).\] At \(z=0\), the formulation must preserve the inactive requirement \(x=0\) and \(t\ge\alpha\). Consequently, the unshifted perspective inequality \(t\ge zf(x/z)\), together with its closed zero-activation slice, represents this inactive epigraph level only when \(\alpha=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite nonzero inactive epigraph level must be interpolated explicitly and retained at zero activation; the usual unshifted perspective corresponds to inactive level zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex. Suppose the original active branch has epigraph set \[E_A=\left\{(x,t):x\in A,\ t\ge f(x)\right\},\] while a perspective reformulation is constructed from the active epigraph set \[E_D=\left\{(x,t):x\in D,\ t\ge f(x)\right\}.\] Equivalence at \(z=1\) requires \(E_A=E_D\). If \(f\) is finite on \(A\cup D\), then \(E_A=E_D\) holds exactly when \(A=D\). Under this finiteness condition, \(A\subsetneq D\) admits forbidden active points, while \(D\subsetneq A\) removes valid active points. Domain constraints must therefore be perspectivized or retained so that the active epigraph is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perspective reformulation must preserve the true active epigraph; when the function is finite on both proposed domains, this requires the domains to be equal.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unshifted Hull Models the Wrong Inactive Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A bounded scalar disjunction explicitly showing the error caused by homogenizing about the origin instead of a nonzero inactive point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[S=\{(x,z):z=0,\ x=1\}\cup\{(x,z):z=1,\ 2\le x\le3\}.\] Its convex hull is \[0\le z\le1,\qquad 1+z\le x\le1+2z.\] By contrast, unshifted homogenization of the active interval gives \(2z\le x\le3z\), whose zero-activation slice is \(x=0\). Thus the unshifted construction represents a disjunction with inactive point zero rather than the intended inactive point one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar example shows that unshifted homogenization replaces a nonzero inactive point by the origin and therefore convexifies a different disjunction.
assumptions_latex: The inactive branch is \((x,z)=(1,0)\).
The active branch has \(z=1\) and \(2\le x\le3\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(S)=\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ 1+z\le x\le1+2z\}\ne\{(x,z):0\le z\le1,\ 2z\le x\le3z\}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonzero inactive point requires translation before perspectivization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the modeled disjunction fixes \(x=x^0\) when \(z=0\), while the active branch at \(z=1\) uses the variable \(x\). An unshifted perspective assumes the inactive point is the origin and is therefore generally inequivalent when \(x^0\ne0\). Introduce \(y=x-(1-z)x^0\). Then \(y=0\) on the inactive branch and \(y=x\) on the active branch, so the perspective must be expressed in \((y,z)\), together with the affine linking equation. Without this translation, the reformulation closes the wrong disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When inactivity fixes a nonzero point, translate that point to the origin before applying the perspective construction.
assumptions_latex: The inactive branch fixes \(x=x^0\).
The active branch corresponds to \(z=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The perspective variable must be \(y=x-(1-z)x^0\), not unshifted \(x\).

children.title: Boundary-Value Inconsistency

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Value Inconsistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-lower-semicontinuous boundary values are changed by closed convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) by \(f(0)=1\) and \(f(x)=x^2\) for \(x>0\). Its epigraph is convex but not closed at \((0,0)\), because \((x_k,f(x_k))\to(0,0)\) for any positive sequence \(x_k\downarrow0\), whereas the declared boundary value is \(f(0)=1\). The lower-semicontinuous closure has value \(0\) at the origin. Consequently, a closed-perspective formulation constructed from the closure does not preserve the original active boundary value at \(x=0\); closure and the declared boundary convention must be reconciled first.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed convexification replaces an inconsistent boundary value by its lower-semicontinuous limit, potentially changing the active branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}f(0)=0\ne f(0)=1\), so closed perspectivization changes the boundary value.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Inactive Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The zero-activation slice is determined by recession and closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex function \(f\), defining its perspective only by \(zf(x/z)\) for \(z>0\) leaves the inactive boundary unspecified and may produce a nonclosed epigraph. The closed perspective is \[f^{\pi}(x,z)=\begin{cases}zf(x/z),&z>0,\\ f^{\infty}(x),&z=0,\\ +\infty,&z<0,\end{cases}\] where \(f^{\infty}\) is the recession function. Thus the inactive slice need not consist only of \(x=0\): every recession direction with finite recession value can occur. Replacing the zero slice by an arbitrary convention can destroy closedness or change the convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closure assigns the recession function at zero activation; forcing an arbitrary inactive slice can omit legitimate limit points or add invalid ones.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed zero-activation value is \(f^{\pi}(x,0)=f^{\infty}(x)\).

children.title: Shared Activation Limits

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A shared indicator remains compatible with componentwise perspectives for additive product geometry without additional joint restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(f(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\). For \(z>0\), \[zf(x_1/z,\ldots,x_m/z)=\sum_{i=1}^m zf_i(x_i/z).\] The equality extends to the closed perspectives at \(z=0\). Thus one common indicator permits an exact sum of component perspectives when the active domain is the corresponding product and no further joint restriction is present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common indicator does not by itself invalidate separate perspective terms: they are exact for an additive function on a product active domain, absent further joint restrictions.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex for every \(i\).
The active function and active domain decompose across the component blocks.
All components use the same activation scale \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^{\pi}(x_1,\ldots,x_m,z)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^{\pi}(x_i,z).

notation.meaning: closed perspective of component function i

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Common-Indicator Decomposition
Shared Activation Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality limits impose a joint activation polytope beyond component perspectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in\{0,1\}^m\) activate \(m\) components and impose the shared limit \(\sum_{i=1}^m z_i\le k\), where \(k\) is an integer with \(0\le k\le m\). Its activation hull is \[\operatorname{conv}\left\{z\in\{0,1\}^m:\sum_{i=1}^m z_i\le k\right\}=\left\{z\in[0,1]^m:\sum_{i=1}^m z_i\le k\right\}.\] Componentwise perspective inequalities constrain each pair \((x_i,z_i)\) but do not imply this shared limit. Any relaxation using those perspectives must retain the joint activation-polytope constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared cardinality limit has its own joint activation hull and is not implied by separately perspectivizing the activated components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation must include \(0\le z_i\le1\) and \(\sum_i z_i\le k\).

children.title: Cross-Component Coupling

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Component Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexification need not commute with intersection by coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{(0,0),(2,0),(1,1)\}\subset\mathbb R^2\) and impose the coupling set \(C=\{(u,v):u=1\}\). Then \(S\cap C=\{(1,1)\}\), so \(\operatorname{conv}(S\cap C)=\{(1,1)\}\). However, \((1,0)=\tfrac12(0,0)+\tfrac12(2,0)\) belongs to \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\cap C\). Hence \[\operatorname{conv}(S\cap C)\subsetneq\operatorname{conv}(S)\cap C.\] Thus convexifying component or disjunctive structure before imposing a cross-component coupling can yield a strict relaxation; the coupled set may require joint valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A concrete finite example shows that separately convexifying a set and then adding coupling can be strictly weaker than joint convexification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(S\cap C)\subsetneq\operatorname{conv}(S)\cap C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(H=\operatorname{conv}(S)\), and suppose the coupling slice is an exposed face \[F=\{x\in H:a^{\mathsf T}x=\beta\},\qquad a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\ \text{for all }x\in H.\] Then \[\operatorname{conv}(S\cap F)=\operatorname{conv}(S)\cap F.\] Thus the noncommutation exhibited by cross-component couplings cannot occur when the coupling selects an exposed face of the already convexified set, although it can occur for a general interior slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexification commutes with a coupling that selects an exposed face, whereas a general slice can produce a strict relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\operatorname{conv}(S)\).
\(F\) is an exposed face of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(S\cap F)=\operatorname{conv}(S)\cap F.

notation.meaning: exposed face selected by the coupling equality
convex hull of the uncoupled set

children.title: Nonseparable Activation Geometry
children.top_down_role: Joint feasible geometry that cannot be represented through independent component perspectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonseparable Activation Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint convex functions require joint rather than componentwise perspectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^{n_1}\times\mathbb R^{n_2}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let one indicator \(z\) activate both arguments. The correct positive-activation perspective is \(zh(x_1/z,x_2/z)\). It can be represented as a sum of separate perspectives only when an appropriate additive decomposition \(h(x_1,x_2)=h_1(x_1)+h_2(x_2)\) holds. For example, if \(h(x_1,x_2)=(x_1-x_2)^2\), then its perspective is \((x_1-x_2)^2/z\), not \(x_1^2/z+x_2^2/z\). Separate terms therefore alter the activated geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A jointly activated nonseparable convex function must be perspectivized jointly; summing component perspectives generally represents a different function.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex.
A common indicator \(z\) activates both arguments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The valid joint expression is \(zh(x_1/z,x_2/z)\); separate perspectives require additive separability.

children.title: Independent Convexification Failure
children.top_down_role: Strength or validity loss from convexifying coupled components separately.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Convexification Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A minimal shared-variable example showing that convexification does not commute with intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}\) be a shared scalar variable, and let its two restrictions be \(C_1=\{0,2\}\) and \(C_2=\{1,2\}\). Their joint feasible set is \(C_1\cap C_2=\{2\}\), so \(\operatorname{conv}(C_1\cap C_2)=\{2\}\). Independent convexification instead gives \(\operatorname{conv}(C_1)=[0,2]\) and \(\operatorname{conv}(C_2)=[1,2]\), whence \(\operatorname{conv}(C_1)\cap\operatorname{conv}(C_2)=[1,2]\). Thus independent component convexification admits every \(x\in[1,2)\), although no such point is a convex combination of jointly feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying two restrictions separately and then intersecting can be strictly weaker than convexifying their joint feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}\) is the scalar variable shared by both restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(C_1\cap C_2)\subsetneq\operatorname{conv}(C_1)\cap\operatorname{conv}(C_2)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Beyond Separable Perspectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint convexification for components coupled through variables or activation decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For component feasible sets \(S_j\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\{0,1\}^p\), define \(S=\bigcap_{j=1}^m S_j\), the separable relaxation \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}=\bigcap_{j=1}^m\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S_j)\), and the joint relaxation \(R_{\mathrm{joint}}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S)\). Then \(R_{\mathrm{joint}}\subseteq R_{\mathrm{sep}}\), possibly strictly. Consequently, a multivariate or combined-disjunction convexification dominates independent perspective convexifications whenever it represents \(R_{\mathrm{joint}}\) or supplies valid inequalities separating points of \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}\setminus R_{\mathrm{joint}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint convexification dominates separate perspective relaxations by retaining inequalities created by shared variables and coupled activation patterns.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is finite and every \(S_j\) uses the same variables \((x,z)\).
The closures of the indicated convex hulls are taken when necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{joint}}\subseteq R_{\mathrm{sep}}\).

notation.meaning: closed convex hull of the joint model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength hierarchy obtained by jointly convexifying progressively larger groups of coupled components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\) be component feasible sets in a common space. For a partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), define \[R_{\mathcal P}=\bigcap_{B\in\mathcal P}\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcap_{j\in B}S_j\right).\] If \(\mathcal P'\) is a coarsening of \(\mathcal P\), then \[\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcap_{j=1}^mS_j\right)\subseteq R_{\mathcal P'}\subseteq R_{\mathcal P}.\] Thus merging component groups before convexification cannot weaken the relaxation; full joint convexification is the strongest member of this grouping hierarchy, although either inclusion may be strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jointly convexifying larger component groups gives a monotone hierarchy of stronger relaxations ending with the full joint hull.
assumptions_latex: The component sets \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\) occupy a common finite-dimensional space.
Convex hulls are closed where necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P'\text{ coarsens }\mathcal P\implies R_{\mathrm{joint}}\subseteq R_{\mathcal P'}\subseteq R_{\mathcal P}.

notation.meaning: partition of component indices into jointly convexified groups
intersection of the closed convex hulls formed groupwise

children.title: Component-Model Intersection
children.top_down_role: Composition through simultaneous enforcement of component feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Component-Model Intersection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection of component formulations through a common block of original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^{r_i}\) be a formulation in shared original variables \(x\) and component auxiliaries \(y_i\), for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Their component-model intersection is \[Q_{\cap}=\{(x,y_1,\ldots,y_m):(x,y_i)\in Q_i\text{ for every }i\}.\] Its relaxation in the original space satisfies \[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\cap})=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_i).\] Thus composition retains exactly the original-variable restrictions common to all projected component formulations, but it need not retain joint convex-hull information absent from every individual component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Component formulations are intersected by requiring one shared original-variable vector to possess a feasible auxiliary lift in every component.
assumptions_latex: Each \(Q_i\) has the same original-variable block \(x\).
The auxiliary blocks \(y_i\) are distinct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\cap})=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_i)\).

children.title: Shared-Variable Linkage
children.top_down_role: Coordination of component formulations through common original-space variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Variable Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus equations linking copies of original variables across component formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose component \(i\) is written with a local copy \(x^i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and feasible region \(Q_i\). Shared-variable linkage introduces a consensus variable \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and imposes \(x^i=x\) for every \(i\). The linked formulation is \[Q_L=\{(x,x^1,\ldots,x^m,y_1,\ldots,y_m):(x^i,y_i)\in Q_i,\ x^i=x\text{ for all }i\}.\] Eliminating the local copies yields \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_L)=\bigcap_i\operatorname{proj}_{x^i}(Q_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared-variable linkage equates local component copies to one consensus vector, thereby intersecting their projected feasible regions.
assumptions_latex: Every local copy \(x^i\) represents the same original quantity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_L)=\bigcap_i\operatorname{proj}_{x^i}(Q_i)\).

notation.meaning: component-local copy of the shared variable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic property of exact consensus linkage among finitely many component formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P_i=\operatorname{proj}_{x^i}(Q_i)\), imposing every consensus equation \(x^i=x\) gives \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_L)=\bigcap_{i=1}^mP_i\). Hence every ordering and parenthesization of the component linkages produces the same projected region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact shared-variable linkage is independent of the order in which components are linked.
assumptions_latex: Every local copy represents the same original-variable vector.
All consensus equalities are imposed exactly.

children.title: Auxiliary-Variable Linkage
children.top_down_role: Coordination through explicit relationships among lifted coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linkage imposed on derived or lifted variables rather than directly on original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_i\subseteq X_i\times Y_i\) be component formulations and let \(T_i:Y_i\to\mathbb{R}^q\) be prescribed linear maps. Auxiliary-variable linkage requires the derived quantities \(T_i y_i\) to agree through a common variable \(u\in\mathbb{R}^q\): \[Q_A=\{(x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_m,y_m,u):(x_i,y_i)\in Q_i,\ T_i y_i=u\text{ for every }i\}.\] The projection of \(Q_A\) consists precisely of component-feasible tuples having mutually compatible auxiliary certificates; this can be smaller than the Cartesian product \(Q_1\times\cdots\times Q_m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary-variable linkage requires selected lifted quantities from different components to share a common value.
assumptions_latex: Each \(T_i\) maps its auxiliary space into the same linkage space \(\mathbb{R}^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,y_1,\ldots,y_m}(Q_A)=\{(x_i,y_i)_i:(x_i,y_i)\in Q_i,\ T_1y_1=\cdots=T_my_m\}\).

children.title: Linkage-Induced Strength Loss
children.top_down_role: Relaxation weakness introduced when component models are connected insufficiently.

knowledge_statements.title: Linkage-Induced Strength Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal component formulations need not remain ideal after independent linking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be component feasible sets and suppose \(Q_i\) is ideal in the sense that \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_i)=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S_i)\). Linking the components only through their common original variables produces \[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\cap})=\bigcap_i\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S_i).\] The convex hull required for the composed integer model is \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\bigcap_i S_i)\), which is contained in the displayed intersection and may be strictly smaller. Hence componentwise ideality does not imply ideality of the linked composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linking ideal component formulations can lose inequalities that are valid only for jointly feasible component configurations.
assumptions_latex: Each component formulation projects to the closed convex hull of its component set.
Components are linked through a common original-variable vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\bigcap_iS_i)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\cap})\), with strict inclusion possible.

notation.meaning: integer feasible set of component i
ideal extended formulation of component i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Empty Joint Set with Nonempty Linked Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal strict-loss example for ideal component formulations linked through common original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_1=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}\) and \(S_2=\{(0,1),(1,0)\}\). Then \(S_1\cap S_2=\varnothing\), whereas \[\operatorname{conv}(S_1)\cap\operatorname{conv}(S_2)=\{(1/2,1/2)\}.\] Thus linking ideal formulations of the components through their common variables admits \((1/2,1/2)\), although the composed integer model is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two ideal component hulls can meet at a fractional point even though the component sets have no common feasible point.
assumptions_latex: The components are linked through both coordinates.
Each component relaxation equals its component convex hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(S_1\cap S_2)=\varnothing\subsetneq\operatorname{conv}(S_1)\cap\operatorname{conv}(S_2)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary sufficient condition under which independent composition loses no convex-hull information.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent convexification commutes with intersection when every component is already closed and convex.
assumptions_latex: Each \(S_i\) is closed and convex.
All components lie in the same original-variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\bigcap_iS_i)=\bigcap_i\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S_i)\).

children.title: Combined-Disjunction Formulations
children.top_down_role: Joint convexification of several logical components.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined-Disjunction Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extended convex-hull formulation for a finite union of polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a positive integer. For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\), let \(A^k\in\mathbb{R}^{m_k\times n}\), \(b^k\in\mathbb{R}^{m_k}\), and let \(P_k=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A^kx\le b^k\}\) be a nonempty polytope. Define the extended system \[Q=\left\{\left(x,(x^k)_{k=1}^K,\lambda\right):x=\sum_{k=1}^Kx^k,\ A^kx^k\le b^k\lambda_k\ (k=1,\ldots,K),\ \sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k=1,\ \lambda_k\ge0\ (k=1,\ldots,K)\right\}.\] Then \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^K P_k)\). Requiring \(\lambda\) to be a unit vector selects one original disjunct, whereas allowing \(\lambda\) to range over the simplex gives the exact convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite union of nonempty polytopes can be convexified jointly by disaggregating the variables and scaling each disjunct with a simplex weight.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\).
For every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\), \(P_k\) is a nonempty polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^K P_k)\).

notation.meaning: variable copy assigned to disjunct k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbounded Disjuncts Require a Closed-Hull Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generator formulation and nonclosed-hull boundary for finite unions of polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_k=\operatorname{conv}\{v^{kj}:j\in V_k\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r^{k\ell}:\ell\in R_k\}\) be nonempty polyhedra. The generator system \[x=\sum_{k,j}v^{kj}\theta_{kj}+\sum_{k,\ell}r^{k\ell}\mu_{k\ell},\qquad \lambda_k=\sum_{j\in V_k}\theta_{kj},\qquad \sum_k\lambda_k=1,\qquad \theta,\mu\ge0\] projects to \[\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_kP_k\right)=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{k,j}\{v^{kj}\}\right)+\operatorname{cone}\left(\bigcup_{k,\ell}\{r^{k\ell}\}\right).\] It represents the unclosed convex hull itself only when that hull is closed, as occurs when the disjuncts have a common recession cone. Closedness cannot be omitted: for \(P_1=\{(0,0)\}\) and \(P_2=\{(t,1):t\ge0\}\), \(\operatorname{conv}(P_1\cup P_2)\) excludes \((t,0)\) for \(t>0\), while its closure contains those points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The natural generator formulation for unbounded polyhedral disjuncts gives the closed convex hull; without a closedness condition it may strictly exceed the ordinary convex hull.
assumptions_latex: The number of disjuncts is finite and positive.
Every \(P_k\) is a nonempty polyhedron with the displayed finite generator representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_kP_k)\), which may strictly contain \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_kP_k)\).

notation.meaning: weight assigned to vertex generator j of disjunct k
coefficient of recession generator ell of disjunct k
total vertex weight assigned to disjunct k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ideality of the Disaggregated Polytope Formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selector integrality at vertices of the accepted bounded combined-disjunction formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions of the accepted polytope formulation \(Q\), \[Q=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{k=1}^K\{(x,(x^h)_h,\lambda):x=x^k\in P_k,\ x^h=0\ (h\ne k),\ \lambda=e_k\}\right).\] Consequently every extreme point of \(Q\) has \(\lambda=e_k\) for some \(k\), so the formulation is ideal with respect to the disjunct selectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every extreme point of the bounded disaggregated convex-hull formulation has a one-hot disjunct selector.
assumptions_latex: Every \(P_k\) is a nonempty polytope.
\(Q\) is the disaggregated system in the accepted seed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ext}(Q)\subseteq\{q:\lambda\in\{e_1,\ldots,e_K\}\}\).

children.title: Partial Model Linkage
children.top_down_role: Composition using only selected links among component formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Model Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A relaxation linking only a selected subset of component quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\) be a positive integer, let \(Q_i\subseteq X_i\times Y_i\) be component formulations, and let \(T_i:Y_i\to\mathbb{R}^q\) map component auxiliaries to quantities that must agree in the fully composed model. Let \(P:\mathbb{R}^q\to\mathbb{R}^s\) be a fixed coordinate projection selecting the retained linkage quantities. Define \[Q_P=\left\{((x_i,y_i))_{i=1}^m\in\prod_{i=1}^mQ_i:PT_1y_1=\cdots=PT_my_m\right\}\] and \[Q_F=\left\{((x_i,y_i))_{i=1}^m\in\prod_{i=1}^mQ_i:T_1y_1=\cdots=T_my_m\right\}.\] Then \(Q_F\subseteq Q_P\). If every feasible tuple of the composed model satisfies the retained equalities defining \(Q_P\), then \(Q_P\) is a valid relaxation of that model; omitting the remaining linkage equations can enlarge its continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial model linkage enforces consensus only on selected coordinates of component linkage quantities, so it contains the corresponding full-linkage formulation and may give a larger relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\).
Every \(T_i\) maps into the common linkage space \(\mathbb{R}^q\).
\(P:\mathbb{R}^q\to\mathbb{R}^s\) is the same coordinate projection for every component.
Every feasible tuple of the composed model satisfies the retained linkage equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_F\subseteq Q_P\).

notation.meaning: common selector for retained linkage coordinates
full-linkage formulation in the same component-tuple space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nestedness of partial-linkage relaxations as additional compatibility coordinates are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,q\}\), and let \(P_S,P_T\) select the corresponding linkage coordinates. For component maps \(T_i:Y_i\to\mathbb R^q\), define \[Q_U=\{((x_i,y_i))_i\in\prod_iQ_i:P_UT_1y_1=\cdots=P_UT_my_m\},\qquad U\in\{S,T\}.\] Then \(Q_T\subseteq Q_S\), and containment is preserved under projection to any common retained variable space. All component maps have the same linkage codomain.
