knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection Can Hide a Nonsimple Lifted Vertex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonsimple lifted vertex whose projection is an original-space interior point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[Q=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,-1,0),(-1,1,0),(1,-1,0),(1,1,0),(0,0,1)\}\subseteq\mathbb R^3\] and \(\pi(x_1,x_2,y)=(x_1,x_2)\). The apex \(v=(0,0,1)\) lies on four side facets and is nonsimple in dimension three, while \(\pi(v)=(0,0)\in\operatorname{int}([-1,1]^2)=\operatorname{int}(\pi(Q))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsimple lifted vertex can project to an ordinary interior point of the original relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is the displayed square pyramid.
\(\pi\) deletes the auxiliary coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\text{ is nonsimple in }Q,\qquad \pi(v)\in\operatorname{int}(\pi(Q)).
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Can Hide a Nonsimple Lifted Vertex

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic geometric degeneracy of a full-dimensional lifted polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a full-dimensional polytope and \(v\) a vertex. The vertex is simple when exactly \(d\) facets contain \(v\), equivalently when its tangent cone has exactly \(d\) extreme rays. It is nonsimple when more than \(d\) facets contain it. This notion depends on the face lattice of \(Q\), not on redundant rows in a chosen inequality description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted vertex is nonsimple when it is incident to more facets than the ambient dimension requires.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is a full-dimensional polytope in \(\mathbb R^d\).
Facet incidence is taken from the polytope rather than a redundant presentation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\text{ is nonsimple}\iff |\{\text{facets of }Q\text{ containing }v\}|>d.
review_flags: Distinct from active-row dependence and standard-form basic-variable degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsimple Lifted Vertex

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Invariance of Intrinsic Lifted-Vertex Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariance of nonsimplicity under invertible affine changes of lifted coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a full-dimensional polytope and let \(T(z)=Mz+q\) with \(M\) nonsingular. The map \(T\) induces a face-lattice isomorphism between \(Q\) and \(T(Q)\); hence \(v\) and \(T(v)\) are incident to the same number of facets. Therefore \(v\) is simple or nonsimple exactly when \(T(v)\) is simple or nonsimple.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible affine coordinate changes preserve intrinsic nonsimplicity of lifted vertices.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is full-dimensional in \(\mathbb R^d\).
\(M\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\text{ is nonsimple in }Q\iff T(v)\text{ is nonsimple in }T(Q).

notation.meaning: invertible affine transformation of lifted space

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Invariance of Intrinsic Lifted-Vertex Degeneracy

assumptions_latex: The lifted relaxation is a polyhedron \(Q=\{z\in\mathbb R^d:Az\le b\}\).
The active set at \(\bar z\in Q\) is \(I(\bar z)=\{i:A_i\bar z=b_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta(\bar z)=|I(\bar z)|-\operatorname{rank}(A_{I(\bar z)})>0\) characterizes active-row degeneracy at \(\bar z\).

notation.meaning: Active constraint indices at the lifted point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: degeneracy is excess active constraints beyond active-normal rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-dependent degeneracy of a lifted polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(\bar z\in Q\), define the active-row degeneracy excess by \[\delta(\bar z):=|I(\bar z)|-\operatorname{rank}(A_{I(\bar z)}).\] The lifted description is active-row degenerate at \(\bar z\) when \(\delta(\bar z)>0\), meaning that its active constraint normals are linearly dependent. This quantity depends on the inequality representation: adding a redundant active row can increase \(\delta(\bar z)\) without changing the projected or lifted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted point is active-row degenerate when its active constraints are linearly dependent; the degeneracy excess counts active rows beyond their rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Lifted Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula correctly detects linear dependence among active rows, but 'active-row degeneracy' is a representation-dependent notion narrower than standard LP degeneracy. A source is needed to establish that this is the intended meaning of the terminal container.

children.title: Basis Stability Under Repeated Solves
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of reusable solver state to degeneracy across successive solves.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict-Margin Robustness of an Optimal Basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient perturbation bounds for retaining a fixed basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with basis \(B=A_{\mathcal B}\), \(x_{\mathcal B}=B^{-1}b\), and \(r_{\mathcal N}=c_{\mathcal N}-A_{\mathcal N}^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}c_{\mathcal B}\). If \(x_{\mathcal B}>0\) and \(r_{\mathcal N}>0\), then for data \(b+\Delta b,c+\Delta c\), the same basis remains optimal whenever \[\|B^{-1}\Delta b\|_\infty<\min_{i\in\mathcal B}(x_{\mathcal B})_i\] and \[\|\Delta c_{\mathcal N}-A_{\mathcal N}^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}\Delta c_{\mathcal B}\|_\infty<\min_{j\in\mathcal N}(r_{\mathcal N})_j.\] Under these strict inequalities the associated basic feasible solution is the unique optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive basic variables and reduced costs give an explicit perturbation neighborhood in which the basis remains optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is nonsingular.
\(c_{\mathcal N}-A_{\mathcal N}^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}c_{\mathcal B}>0\).
Only \(b\) and \(c\) are perturbed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ remains optimal under the displayed strict perturbation bounds}.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Margin Robustness of an Optimal Basis

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on inferring stable returned bases from unchanged LP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min\ 0\quad\text{s.t.}\quad x_1+x_2=1,\quad x_1,x_2\ge0,\] both singleton bases \(\{x_1\}\) and \(\{x_2\}\) are optimal. Thus repeated solution of the identical LP may return different optimal bases when initialization or tie-breaking differs, even though the feasible set and optimal value are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple optimal bases allow identical repeated LPs to return different basis identities.
assumptions_latex: The solver may choose either optimal basis.
No deterministic basis-selection convention is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B^t\ne B^{t-1}\text{ may occur although the LP data are unchanged}.

notation.meaning: basis returned on repeated solve t

review_flags: This example concerns nonunique optimal solutions, not primal degeneracy at a fixed basic feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Optima Prevent Returned-Basis Stability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Margin Eliminates a Uniform Basis-Retention Radius
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of strict-margin basis stability under objective perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x_1+x_2=1,\ x\ge0\}\), take basis \(\mathcal B=\{1\}\) and \(c=(0,0)\). Its nonbasic reduced cost is zero. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the perturbation \(\Delta c=(0,-\varepsilon)\) has infinity norm \(\varepsilon\) and makes the reduced cost of \(x_2\) negative, so \(\mathcal B\) is no longer optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero reduced-cost margin can allow arbitrarily small objective perturbations to destroy basis optimality.
assumptions_latex: The LP is in standard minimization form.
The candidate basis is \(\mathcal B=\{1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\varepsilon>0\ \exists\Delta c,\ \|\Delta c\|_\infty=\varepsilon:\ \mathcal B\text{ is not optimal for }c+\Delta c.
review_flags: This establishes absence of a guaranteed open stability neighborhood, not failure under every perturbation.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Margin Eliminates a Uniform Basis-Retention Radius

assumptions_latex: For each parameter \(\theta\), consider \(\min\{c(\theta)^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b(\theta),\ x\ge0\}\) with fixed \(A\).
The square nonsingular submatrix \(B=A_{\mathcal B}\) specifies a candidate basis, with complement \(\mathcal N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(B^{-1}b(\theta)\ge0\) and \(c_{\mathcal N}(\theta)-A_{\mathcal N}^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}c_{\mathcal B}(\theta)\ge0\), then \(B\) remains optimal at \(\theta\).

notation.meaning: Basic matrix formed from columns indexed by the basis

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual feasibility test for retaining one LP basis.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Preliminaries from linear algebra, matrix theory, and Euclidean geometry p. 4
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The basis \(B\) is stable on a parameter set \(\Theta\) if, for every \(\theta\in\Theta\), \[B^{-1}b(\theta)\ge0\quad\text{and}\quad c_{\mathcal N}(\theta)-A_{\mathcal N}^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}c_{\mathcal B}(\theta)\ge0.\] The first inequalities give primal feasibility of the associated basic solution; the second give nonnegative reduced costs. Hence the same basis is optimal throughout \(\Theta\), although the basic solution or objective value may vary with \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basis remains optimal across repeated LPs when its basic solution stays feasible and all nonbasic reduced costs stay nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Stability Under Repeated Solves

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Preliminaries from linear algebra, matrix theory, and Euclidean geometry p. 4
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal-feasibility and reduced-cost condition is mathematically correct for a standard-form minimization LP, but the cited linear-algebra preliminaries do not specifically support simplex basis optimality or parametric basis stability.

children.title: Formulation Reliability Engineering
children.top_down_role: Formulation-level checks and transformations required for correctness, strength, and numerical reliability.

children.title: Lifted-Model Validation Certificates
children.top_down_role: Checks for missing links, unintended projections, and incorrect auxiliary-variable coupling.

children.title: Projection Correctness
children.top_down_role: Checks that the lifted representation projects to the intended feasible set.

assumptions_latex: The intended feasible set is \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
The lifted formulation is \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\) in variables \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate establishes \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=X\).

notation.meaning: Projection of the lifted set onto original variables
Witness assigning auxiliary variables to each intended feasible point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-inclusion certificate for exact lifted projection.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 The condensed formulation p. 9
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A projection-correctness certificate consists of two verifiable assertions: \[(x,y)\in Q\Longrightarrow x\in X,\qquad x\in X\Longrightarrow (x,s(x))\in Q\] for some explicitly specified witness map \(s:X\to\mathbb R^p\). The first assertion certifies \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\subseteq X\); the witness certifies \(X\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\). Together they certify the exact identity \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection correctness is certified by showing every lifted feasible point projects into the original set and every original feasible point has a feasible lift.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Correctness

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 The condensed formulation p. 9
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Linking Constraint Completeness
children.top_down_role: Coverage of required connections between original variables and auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Point witnesses for either direction of failure of a proposed linking system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be the base feasible set, \(T\subseteq B\) the intended lifted relation, and \(L\) the set satisfying the proposed links. Linking completeness fails if and only if at least one witness set is nonempty: \[(B\cap L)\setminus T\ne\varnothing\quad\text{or}\quad T\setminus L\ne\varnothing.\] A point in the first set certifies an underrestrictive link; a point in the second certifies an overrestrictive link.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surviving unintended tuple certifies a weak or missing link, while an intended tuple rejected by the links certifies an overrestrictive link.
assumptions_latex: The intended relation satisfies \(T\subseteq B\).
The proposed linking constraints define \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\cap L\ne T\iff ((B\cap L)\setminus T)\cup(T\setminus L)\ne\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Intended lifted tuples rejected by the links.

knowledge_statements.title: Witnesses of Linking Incompleteness

assumptions_latex: The base constraints define \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\).
The intended lifted feasible relation is \(T\subseteq B\), and the linking constraints define \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linking constraints are complete exactly when \(B\cap L=T\).

notation.meaning: Set satisfying constraints other than the linking system

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: completeness means exact recovery of the intended relation after adding links
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-set criterion for completeness of linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linking system is complete relative to \(B\) and \(T\) when \[B\cap L=T.\] Equivalently, it must satisfy both \(T\subseteq B\cap L\), so no intended lifted tuple is removed, and \(B\cap L\subseteq T\), so no tuple violating the intended relation survives. Projection equality alone is insufficient for this condition because incorrect auxiliary values may survive while producing the same original-variable projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linking constraints are complete when adding them to the base constraints yields exactly the intended lifted relation, not merely the correct projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Linking Constraint Completeness

children.title: Auxiliary Coupling Integrity
children.top_down_role: Checks for unintended freedom or incorrect coupling among auxiliary components.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Projection Does Not Ensure Coupling Integrity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal separation between original-variable projection correctness and fiberwise auxiliary correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), let \(Y^*(x)=\{x\}\), and define \[Q=[0,1]^2.\] Then \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=X\), but \[Q_x=[0,1]\ne\{x\}=Y^*(x)\] for every \(x\in X\). Hence exact projection does not imply auxiliary coupling integrity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unit square has the correct x-projection but incorrect auxiliary fibers, so projection correctness does not ensure coupling integrity.
assumptions_latex: The intended original set is \(X=[0,1]\).
The intended auxiliary relation is \(y=x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=X\quad\text{but}\quad Q_x\ne Y^*(x)\ \text{for every }x\in X.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Projection Does Not Ensure Coupling Integrity
Auxiliary Coupling Integrity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fiberwise validation of original-to-auxiliary coupling over the intended original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(Y^*(x)\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be nonempty for every \(x\in X\), and let \(Q\subseteq X\times\mathbb R^p\). For each \(x\in X\), define the implemented fiber \(Q_x:=\{y\in\mathbb R^p:(x,y)\in Q\}\). Auxiliary coupling integrity holds when \[Q_x=Y^*(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.\] Thus every intended auxiliary realization is admitted and every admitted realization has the intended relationship to \(x\). Under the stated domain restriction and nonempty-fiber assumption, this condition also implies \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=X\), while exact projection alone does not imply fiber equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary coupling has integrity when, for every intended original feasible point, the implemented auxiliary values are exactly the intended auxiliary values; the lifted set is also restricted to intended original points.
assumptions_latex: The intended original feasible set is \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
For every \(x\in X\), the intended auxiliary fiber \(Y^*(x)\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is nonempty.
The implemented lifted set satisfies \(Q\subseteq X\times\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Auxiliary coupling integrity holds exactly when \(\{y\in\mathbb R^p:(x,y)\in Q\}=Y^*(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fiber equality formalizes exact auxiliary coupling
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Unintended Projection Effects
children.top_down_role: Projection defects that admit invalid points or exclude intended points.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Overrestrictive Linking Can Shrink a Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal projection loss caused by an incorrect auxiliary link.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[Q^*:=\{(x,y):0\le x\le1,\ y=x\},\] so \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q^*)=[0,1]\). Adding the incorrect link \(y=0\) gives \[Q:=\{(x,y):0\le x\le1,\ y=x,\ y=0\},\] and therefore \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the incorrect link y=0 to y=x shrinks the x-projection from the unit interval to zero.
assumptions_latex: The intended lifted relation is \(y=x\) for \(0\le x\le1\).
The faulty formulation additionally imposes \(y=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\{0\}\subsetneq[0,1]=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q^*).
knowledge_statements.title: Overrestrictive Linking Can Shrink a Projection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive classification into admitted and excluded original-variable points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For target \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and lifted set \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\), define \[E^+(Q;X):=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\setminus X,\qquad E^-(Q;X):=X\setminus\operatorname{proj}_x(Q).\] The projection is correct if and only if both sets are empty. A point of \(E^+\) is admitted unintentionally; a point of \(E^-\) has no feasible lift. Both sets may be nonempty when the projections are incomparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection defects consist exactly of extra projected points and intended points lacking a lift; correctness requires both defect sets to be empty.
assumptions_latex: The intended original-variable set is \(X\).
The implemented lifted feasible set is \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=X\iff E^+(Q;X)=E^-(Q;X)=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Classification of Projection Defects

assumptions_latex: The intended lift enforces \(y=x\) and \(y\ge\tfrac12\) for \(0\le x\le1\).
The faulty lift omits the linking equality \(y=x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q^*)=[\tfrac12,1]\) but \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=[0,1]\).

notation.meaning: Faulty lifted set with the link omitted

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projection identities follow directly by eliminating the auxiliary variable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete projection enlargement caused by an omitted link.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[Q^*:=\{(x,y):0\le x\le1,\ 0\le y\le1,\ y=x,\ y\ge\tfrac12\}.\] Its intended projection is \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q^*)=[\tfrac12,1]\). If the linking equality is omitted, the faulty set becomes \[Q:=\{(x,y):0\le x\le1,\ 0\le y\le1,\ y\ge\tfrac12\},\] whose projection is \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=[0,1]\). Thus missing auxiliary coupling admits unintended original-variable points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting the link y=x lets every x between zero and one survive, enlarging the intended projection from one-half-to-one to zero-to-one.
knowledge_statements.title: Unintended Projection Effects

children.title: Reformulation Parameter Calibration
children.top_down_role: Domain and coefficient tightening for implications, envelopes, and on-off structures.

children.title: Variable Bound Calibration
children.top_down_role: Selection of valid, informative domains for original and auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Farkas Certificates for Polyhedral Variable Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier certificates for coordinate bounds implied by a nonempty linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq b\}\) be nonempty. A vector \(\lambda\geq0\) satisfying
\[
\lambda^{\mathsf T}A=e_i^{\mathsf T},\qquad \lambda^{\mathsf T}b\leq u_i
\]
certifies \(x_i\leq u_i\) for every \(x\in R\). Likewise, \(\mu\geq0\) with
\[
\mu^{\mathsf T}A=-e_i^{\mathsf T},\qquad \mu^{\mathsf T}b\leq-\ell_i
\]
certifies \(x_i\geq\ell_i\). Conversely, every valid finite bound of either form admits the corresponding multiplier certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative combinations of model rows certify polyhedrally implied variable bounds, and every valid finite coordinate bound has such a certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(R=\{x:Ax\leq b\}\) is nonempty.
The asserted coordinate bound is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed nonnegative multipliers are necessary and sufficient certificates for polyhedrally implied coordinate bounds.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative row multipliers certifying upper and lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Certificates for Polyhedral Variable Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safe Bounds from Outer Relaxations and Integrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and rounding rules for practically computed variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). If
\[
\underline\ell_i:=\inf_{x\in R}x_i,\qquad \overline u_i:=\sup_{x\in R}x_i
\]
are finite, then \(\underline\ell_i\leq x_i\leq\overline u_i\) is valid for every \(x\in X\), though it need not be tight over \(X\). If additionally \(x_i\in\mathbb Z\), then
\[
\lceil\underline\ell_i\rceil\leq x_i\leq\lfloor\overline u_i\rfloor
\]
remains valid. An unbounded relaxation extremum supplies no finite bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing over an outer relaxation gives safe, possibly loose bounds; bounds on an integer variable may then be rounded inward.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq R\).
Each relaxation extremum used as a finite bound is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxation extrema give valid bounds on \(X\), and ceiling or floor strengthening preserves validity for an integer coordinate.

notation.meaning: Outer relaxation containing the feasible set.
Coordinate extrema over the outer relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Bounds from Outer Relaxations and Integrality

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
For coordinate \(i\), both \(\inf_{x\in X}x_i\) and \(\sup_{x\in X}x_i\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tight valid bounds are \(\ell_i^*=\inf_{x\in X}x_i\) and \(u_i^*=\sup_{x\in X}x_i\).

notation.meaning: Tight lower bound for variable i over the feasible set
Tight upper bound for variable i over the feasible set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tight coordinate bounds are coordinatewise infima and suprema
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tight coordinatewise bounds over the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\ell_i^*:=\inf_{x\in X}x_i,\qquad u_i^*:=\sup_{x\in X}x_i.\] Bounds \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\) are valid for every \(x\in X\) exactly when \(\ell_i\le\ell_i^*\) and \(u_i\ge u_i^*\). Variable-bound calibration is tight when \(\ell_i=\ell_i^*\) and \(u_i=u_i^*\). Computing these values amounts to two optimization problems over \(X\), with infimum or supremum retained when attainment fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Calibrate a variable's tight valid bounds by minimizing and maximizing that coordinate over the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Bound Calibration

children.title: Implication Coefficient Calibration
children.top_down_role: Coefficient selection for implication-based formulation components.

assumptions_latex: The implication is \(z=1\Longrightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\), where \(z\in\{0,1\}\).
The domain \(X\) is nonempty and \(\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The smallest nonnegative valid coefficient is \(M^*=\max\{0,\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tight big-M calibration for one linear implication.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.4 The smooth binary formulation p. 11
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Encode the implication by \[a^{\mathsf T}x\le b+M(1-z).\] For \(z=1\), this is the required inequality. For \(z=0\), validity over \(X\) requires \(M\ge a^{\mathsf T}x-b\) for every \(x\in X\). Consequently, among nonnegative coefficients, the tight calibration is \[M^*:=\max\left\{0,\sup_{x\in X}(a^{\mathsf T}x-b)\right\}.\] Every \(M\ge M^*\) is valid, while every \(0\le M<M^*\) excludes some point of \(X\) when the supremum violation exceeds \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linear indicator implication, the tight nonnegative big-M equals the largest possible inactive-state violation over the variable domain, truncated below at zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Implication Coefficient Calibration

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.4 The smooth binary formulation p. 11
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed-Form Box Calibration of a Linear Implication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact evaluation of a linear implication coefficient over a finite variable box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(X=[\ell,u]\) has finite componentwise bounds. For
\[
z=1\Longrightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b,
\]
the tight nonnegative coefficient in \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b+M(1-z)\) is
\[
M^*=\max\left\{0,\sum_{j:a_j\geq0}a_ju_j+\sum_{j:a_j<0}a_j\ell_j-b\right\}.
\]
For several implication rows, applying this formula separately yields tight row-specific coefficients. Replacing them by their common maximum remains valid but can weaken the continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over a box, maximize each implication row by selecting an endpoint according to the coefficient sign, yielding its exact row-specific big-M.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_j\leq u_j\) are finite for every coordinate.
The inactive-state domain is the full box \(X=[\ell,u]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sign-based expression equals the smallest nonnegative valid coefficient \(M^*\) for the row.

notation.meaning: Finite componentwise lower and upper bounds.
Tight nonnegative implication coefficient over the box.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Form Box Calibration of a Linear Implication

children.title: Envelope Coefficient Calibration
children.top_down_role: Parameter choices governing relaxation envelopes over calibrated domains.

assumptions_latex: Variables satisfy finite bounds \(\ell_x\le x\le u_x\) and \(\ell_y\le y\le u_y\).
The auxiliary variable \(w\) represents the product \(xy\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The four calibrated inequalities give the convex hull of \(\{(x,y,w):w=xy\}\) over the bounding rectangle.

notation.meaning: Lower and upper bounds for the two factors.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: McCormick-envelope coefficients follow directly from finite factor bounds; dedicated source certification remains pending
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bilinear-envelope calibration on a bounded rectangle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \((x,y)\in[\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\), calibrate the linear envelope for \(w=xy\) using the actual finite bounds. The resulting formulation is
\[
w\ge \ell_x y+\ell_y x-\ell_x\ell_y,\qquad w\ge u_x y+u_y x-u_xu_y,
\]
\[
w\le u_x y+\ell_y x-u_x\ell_y,\qquad w\le \ell_x y+u_y x-\ell_xu_y.
\]
These coefficients are determined by the four corners of the bounding rectangle. Replacing any bound by a looser valid bound preserves validity but can enlarge the continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the true finite factor bounds in the four McCormick inequalities; looser bounds remain valid but generally weaken the product relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Coefficient Calibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-rectangle McCormick representation is mathematically precise, the representation kind fits the calibration leaf, and the TeX is properly delimited. However, the convex-hull and relaxation-strength claims have no inspectable citation; standard-field rationale alone does not resolve the missing source certification here.

children.title: On-Off Parameter Calibration
children.top_down_role: Parameter choices controlling activated or deactivated formulation regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise extension of scalar on-off calibration to a bounded box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
S=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,1):\ell\leq x\leq u\},
\]
where inequalities are componentwise and \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\) are finite. Then
\[
\operatorname{conv}(S)=\{(x,z):\ell_jz\leq x_j\leq u_jz\ (j=1,\ldots,n),\ 0\leq z\leq1\}.
\]
Thus a single activation variable shared by a box of activities uses each coordinate's exact active-state bounds as its hull coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a vector activity in a box, scaling every coordinate's exact bounds by the common activation variable gives the convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\) are finite and satisfy \(\ell\leq u\).
The inactive activity is the origin and one common binary variable activates the entire box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(S)=\{(x,z):\ell z\leq x\leq uz,\ 0\leq z\leq1\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Box On-Off Hull Calibration

assumptions_latex: The intended set is \(S=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,1):\ell\le x\le u\}\).
The constants \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R\) are finite and satisfy \(\ell\le u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(\ell z\le x\le uz\), together with \(0\le z\le1\), describe \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\).

notation.meaning: Binary activation variable in the on-off set and its continuous relaxation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar bounded on-off disjunction with binary activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the scalar on-off set
\[
S=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,1):\ell\le x\le u\}.
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{conv}(S)=\{(x,z):\ell z\le x\le uz,\ 0\le z\le1\}.
\]
Thus exact active-state bounds give the convex-hull coefficients. Replacing \(\ell\) by a smaller value or \(u\) by a larger value gives an outer relaxation containing \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\), but it does not preserve the same integer-feasible set unless other constraints separately enforce the original active-state bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact active-state bounds give the convex hull of the scalar on-off set. Wider coefficients give an outer relaxation and preserve the original integer set only when separate constraints enforce the original active bounds.

children.title: Formulation Granularity Design
children.top_down_role: Choice of shared or separated variables and constraints to balance size and strength.

children.title: Aggregated Variable Design
children.top_down_role: Shared-variable representations that prioritize compactness across related structures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines replacement of detailed variables by linear summaries and exactness relative to retained variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r\) denote variables whose feasible set \(F\) must be retained, and let \(x\in\mathbb R^I\) be detailed formulation variables. An aggregated-variable design replaces some uses of \(x\) by a lower-dimensional summary
\[
y=Tx,
\]
and formulates a set \(G\) in \((r,y)\) and any remaining auxiliaries. It is exact relative to \(r\) when
\[
\operatorname{proj}_r(G)=F,
\]
and is a valid relaxation when \(F\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_r(G)\). Aggregation can reduce explicit granularity but identifies detailed vectors lying in the same fiber of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregated design replaces detailed variables by fewer linear summaries and is exact when the resulting formulation preserves the intended retained-variable projection.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a specified linear aggregation map with fewer rows than detailed coordinates.
\(F\) is the intended feasible set in retained-variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness requires \(\operatorname{proj}_r(G)=F\); relaxation validity requires \(F\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_r(G)\).
review_flags: Clarifies the deferred seed candidate by separating retained variables from detailed variables that may be removed.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregated Variable Design

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when membership in a detailed set can depend only on an aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R^q\) and \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^I\). A detailed feasible set can be described solely through \(Tx\), meaning \(F=T^{-1}(S)\) for some \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^q\), if and only if it is saturated on the fibers of \(T\):
\[
Tx=Tx'\Longrightarrow(x\in F\iff x'\in F).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
F=T^{-1}(T(F)).
\]
Therefore, a pair \(x,x'\) with \(Tx=Tx'\) and opposite feasibility certifies that an aggregate-only description cannot be exact without retaining additional distinguishing information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate-only exactness is possible exactly when feasibility is constant on every fiber of the aggregation map.
assumptions_latex: \(T:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R^q\) is the chosen aggregation map.
The proposed description may test a detailed vector only through \(Tx\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Aggregate-only exactness is equivalent to \(F=T^{-1}(T(F))\).

notation.meaning: union of all aggregation fibers meeting F
directions invisible to the aggregation map

knowledge_statements.title: Fiber-Saturation Boundary for Aggregate-Only Feasibility

children.title: Disaggregated Variable Design
children.top_down_role: Separated-variable representations that expose component-specific structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines separated component variables, linking, projection exactness, and the boundary on strength comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A disaggregated-variable design introduces component variables \(x_i\) for \(i\in I\), imposes component-specific constraints, and links them to retained variables, commonly through
\[
y=\sum_{i\in I}x_i.
\]
If \(F\) is the intended feasible set for retained variables \(r\), and \(G\) is the lifted feasible set in \((r,(x_i)_{i\in I})\), the design is exact when
\[
\operatorname{proj}_r(G)=F.
\]
For an aggregate relaxation \(H\), disaggregation is at least as strong only when \(\operatorname{proj}_r(G)\subseteq H\); separated variables alone do not imply this inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregation exposes component-specific variables linked to retained aggregates; exactness and strength are determined by projection, not by separation alone.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
\(G\) is the lifted feasible set after component-specific constraints and linking are imposed.
\(F\) is the intended retained-variable feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness requires \(\operatorname{proj}_r(G)=F\), while strength relative to \(H\) requires \(\operatorname{proj}_r(G)\subseteq H\).
review_flags: Replaces the deferred seed candidate with a publishable standard-unsourced definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Disaggregated Variable Design

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical exact representation of an aggregate as a sum of independently constrained contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite set \(I\), let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and define
\[
Y=\sum_{i\in I}X_i=\left\{\sum_{i\in I}x_i:x_i\in X_i\ \forall i\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
x_i\in X_i\quad(i\in I),\qquad y=\sum_{i\in I}x_i
\]
is an exact lifted representation:
\[
\operatorname{proj}_y\left\{(y,(x_i)_{i\in I}):x_i\in X_i,\ y=\sum_i x_i\right\}=Y.
\]
If each \(X_i\) has a linear or mixed-integer formulation, inserting those component formulations yields a corresponding disaggregated formulation of \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separately constrained contribution variables linked by summation exactly represent the Minkowski sum of their component sets.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
Each \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is represented in its own variable block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_y\{(y,x):x_i\in X_i,\ y=\sum_i x_i\}=\sum_iX_i\).

notation.meaning: Minkowski sum of the component sets

knowledge_statements.title: Minkowski-Sum Disaggregation

children.title: Hybrid Granularity Design
children.top_down_role: Mixed representations using selective sharing across formulation components.

assumptions_latex: The finite index set \(I\) is partitioned into nonempty blocks \(\mathcal P\).
The original feasible set is \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and the hybrid representation has a specified recovery map \(\pi_{\mathcal P}\) into the original-variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hybrid representation is exact when \(\pi_{\mathcal P}(G_{\mathcal P})=F\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the hybrid representation.
Recovery or projection map from the hybrid representation to original-variable space.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: blockwise aggregation interpolates between aggregate and detailed representations only after retained-detail rules and a recovery map are specified
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise mixture of aggregated and disaggregated variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a partition \(\mathcal P\) of \(I\), a hybrid-granularity design may introduce block aggregates
\[
y_B=\sum_{i\in B}x_i\qquad(B\in\mathcal P)
\]
while retaining selected component variables or component-level constraints in specified blocks. Let \(G_{\mathcal P}\) be the hybrid feasible set and let \(\pi_{\mathcal P}\) be its specified recovery map into the original-variable space containing \(F\). The representation is exact when
\[
\pi_{\mathcal P}(G_{\mathcal P})=F.
\]
If no additional detail is retained, \(\mathcal P=\{I\}\) gives one aggregate block and the singleton partition gives fully detailed blocks. Refining \(\mathcal P\) guarantees a stronger relaxation only when the refined construction preserves the constraints of the coarser construction and yields a nested recovered relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid granularity uses block aggregates together with selected retained detail. Exactness is defined through a specified recovery map, and partition refinement strengthens a relaxation only under an explicit nesting condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Granularity Design

children.title: Size–Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes determining how representation granularity affects formulation size and relaxation strength.

assumptions_latex: Three valid formulations represent the same integer-feasible set in the original variables.
Their continuous relaxations satisfy \(P_D\subseteq P_H\subseteq P_A\) after projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projected bound strength improves from aggregated to hybrid to disaggregated, while formulation size need not improve in the same direction.

notation.meaning: Projected continuous relaxations of disaggregated, hybrid, and aggregated formulations.

auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional size-strength ordering under projected relaxation inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a minimization problem, if projected continuous relaxations obey
\[
P_D\subseteq P_H\subseteq P_A,
\]
then their relaxation values satisfy
\[
\inf_{x\in P_A}c^{\mathsf T}x\le \inf_{x\in P_H}c^{\mathsf T}x\le \inf_{x\in P_D}c^{\mathsf T}x.
\]
Thus the disaggregated representation is at least as strong by bound value, and the aggregated representation is at most as strong. This ordering is conditional on the displayed inclusions. Formulation sizes \(s(D),s(H),s(A)\), measured by variables, constraints, or nonzeros, are independent criteria; no universal ordering of computational time follows from either size or relaxation strength alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When projected relaxations are nested, disaggregation gives the strongest minimization bound, but model size and solution time obey no universal ordering.
knowledge_statements.title: Size–Strength Regimes

children.title: Auxiliary Symmetry Control
children.top_down_role: Design choices that avoid equivalent lifted representations and redundant search alternatives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lexicographic Ordering of Interchangeable Auxiliary Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A standard orbit-representative restriction for fully interchangeable auxiliary blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(G\) is invariant under every permutation of auxiliary blocks \(u^1,\ldots,u^k\), and these permutations fix all retained variables. Then imposing
\[
u^1\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}u^2\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}u^k
\]
preserves the retained-variable projection because every permutation orbit contains an ordered representative. Ties may leave multiple representatives. The restriction is not valid under this rationale when the blocks are not genuinely interchangeable or when the permutation changes retained-variable semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographically ordering fully interchangeable auxiliary blocks removes equivalent representatives without changing the retained-variable projection.
assumptions_latex: Auxiliary blocks \(u^1,\ldots,u^k\) have a common ordered domain.
Every block permutation preserves feasibility and fixes retained variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lexicographically ordered restriction has the same retained-variable projection as \(G\).
review_flags: Replaces the deferred seed candidate with a publishable standard-unsourced statement.
knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Ordering of Interchangeable Auxiliary Blocks

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orbit-Hitting Criterion for Auxiliary Symmetry Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes projection-preserving restrictions for symmetries acting only in auxiliary fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\subseteq X\times U\) be a lifted feasible set. Let \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{aux}}\) be a group of bijections of \(U\) such that
\[
(x,u)\in G\iff(x,\gamma u)\in G
\]
for every \(\gamma\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{aux}}\). If \(D\subseteq U\) intersects every \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{aux}}\)-orbit occurring in every nonempty feasible fiber \(G_x=\{u:(x,u)\in G\}\), then
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x(G\cap(X\times D))=\operatorname{proj}_x(G).
\]
Thus meeting every feasible auxiliary orbit is sufficient for valid symmetry control; selecting a unique representative is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restriction on auxiliary variables preserves the retained-variable projection whenever it meets every feasible orbit of an auxiliary-only symmetry group.
assumptions_latex: \(G\subseteq X\times U\) is a lifted feasible set.
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{aux}}\) acts bijectively on auxiliary variables, fixes retained variables, and preserves feasibility.
\(D\) meets every feasible auxiliary orbit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(G\cap(X\times D))=\operatorname{proj}_x(G)\).

notation.meaning: feasible auxiliary fiber over retained point x

knowledge_statements.title: Orbit-Hitting Criterion for Auxiliary Symmetry Control

assumptions_latex: Auxiliary blocks \(u^1,\ldots,u^k\in\mathbb R^m\) are interchangeable under every permutation.
Permuting these blocks leaves all retained variables and feasibility unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lexicographic ordering selects at least one representative from every auxiliary permutation orbit without changing the retained-variable projection.

notation.meaning: Permutation group on the auxiliary blocks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic control of interchangeable auxiliary blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a lifted feasible set \(G\) is invariant under \(S_k\) acting by permutation of the auxiliary blocks \(u^1,\ldots,u^k\), and this action fixes every retained variable. Auxiliary symmetry may be controlled by imposing
\[
u^1\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}u^2\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}\cdots\succeq_{\mathrm{lex}}u^k.
\]
For every point of \(G\), some permutation of its auxiliary blocks satisfies this ordering. Consequently, adding the ordering leaves the projection onto retained variables unchanged while removing all but the tied ordered representatives of each permutation orbit. The condition is invalid if the blocks are not genuinely interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lexicographically order truly interchangeable auxiliary blocks to remove equivalent lifted representations while preserving the projection onto original variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Symmetry Control

children.title: Numerical Stability Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Coefficient and representation choices affecting numerical stability.

children.title: Coefficient Scaling
children.top_down_role: Magnitude normalization choices for variables, constraints, and linking coefficients.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which diagonal coordinate scaling preserves an integer-coordinate lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(x=D_cy\) with positive diagonal \(D_c=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\), the requirement \(x_j\in\mathbb Z\) becomes \[d_jy_j\in\mathbb Z,\] not generally \(y_j\in\mathbb Z\). Declaring \(y_j\) integer produces the same full lattice in the \(x_j\)-coordinate only when \(d_j\mathbb Z=\mathbb Z\), which for positive real \(d_j\) holds exactly when \(d_j=1\). Other scalings remain exact only when the transformed lattice or an equivalent discrete domain is enforced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling an integer variable changes its lattice; simply declaring the scaled coordinate integer is equivalent only for positive unit scaling unless the transformed discrete domain is enforced.
assumptions_latex: The substitution is \(x=D_cy\) with positive diagonal \(D_c\).
Coordinate \(x_j\) ranges over the integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_j\in\mathbb Z\iff d_jy_j\in\mathbb Z;\qquad d_j\mathbb Z=\mathbb Z\iff d_j=1.

notation.meaning: Positive scaling factor for coordinate j.
Image in x-space of integer values assigned to y_j.

assumptions_latex: The linear system is \(Ax\le b\).
The diagonal matrices \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) have strictly positive diagonal entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive row and column scaling yields an equivalent exact-arithmetic system with matrix \(D_rAD_c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal scaling of linear constraints and variables.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Preliminaries from linear algebra, matrix theory, and Euclidean geometry p. 4
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) be positive diagonal matrices and substitute \(x=D_cy\). Multiplying each inequality by its positive row factor gives
\[
D_rAD_cy\le D_rb.
\]
The map \(y=D_c^{-1}x\) is bijective, so the scaled and unscaled systems represent the same feasible points after variable conversion in exact arithmetic. Row scaling alone does not change the feasible set in \(x\). Scaling should reduce harmful coefficient disparities without making nonzero coefficients numerically indistinguishable from zero or changing integrality conventions for scaled variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row scaling and invertible diagonal variable scaling preserve exact feasibility while changing coefficient magnitudes and numerical behavior.

children.title: Representation Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Conditioning effects arising from lifted variables, redundant structure, or coefficient patterns.

assumptions_latex: The representation matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full column rank.
Conditioning is measured in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The spectral condition number is \(\kappa_2(A)=\sigma_{\max}(A)/\sigma_{\min}(A)\) and quantifies worst-case linear sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditioning of a full-column-rank linear representation.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Preliminaries from linear algebra, matrix theory, and Euclidean geometry p. 4
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a full-column-rank matrix \(A\), its Euclidean representation condition number is
\[
\kappa_2(A)=\lVert A\rVert_2\lVert A^{\dagger}\rVert_2
=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)}{\sigma_{\min}(A)}.
\]
It measures the worst-case amplification associated with solving or inverting the represented linear relation, relative to the chosen coordinates and norm. If \(A\) loses column rank, set \(\kappa_2(A)=+\infty\). Because diagonal row or column scaling changes singular values, conditioning belongs to a representation rather than solely to its exact feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representation conditioning is the ratio of largest to smallest singular value; it depends on coordinates and becomes infinite at rank loss.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Conditioning

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Preliminaries from linear algebra, matrix theory, and Euclidean geometry p. 4
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-conditioning degradation caused by replacing a full-column-rank relation with its normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full column rank, then \(A^{\mathsf T}A\) is positive definite and \[\kappa_2(A^{\mathsf T}A)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)^2}{\sigma_{\min}(A)^2}=\kappa_2(A)^2.\] Thus the normal-equations representation squares the Euclidean spectral condition number.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a full-column-rank matrix, the normal-equations representation has the square of the original spectral condition number.
assumptions_latex: The representation matrix \(A\) has full column rank.
Conditioning is measured in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(A^{\mathsf T}A)=\kappa_2(A)^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Condition Squaring in Normal Equations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orthogonal and Scalar Invariance of Spectral Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformations that leave the Euclidean spectral condition number unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full column rank, let \(\alpha\ne0\), and let \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) and \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be orthogonal. Then \[\kappa_2(\alpha UAV)=\kappa_2(A).\] Uniform nonzero scaling and orthogonal row or column coordinate changes preserve spectral conditioning, whereas general nonsingular diagonal scaling need not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform scaling and orthogonal coordinate changes preserve the spectral condition number, while nonuniform diagonal scaling can change it.
assumptions_latex: The matrix \(A\) has full column rank.
Matrices \(U\) and \(V\) are orthogonal.
The scalar \(\alpha\) is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(\alpha UAV)=\kappa_2(A).
knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonal and Scalar Invariance of Spectral Conditioning

children.title: Representation-Induced Instability
children.top_down_role: Numerical failure regimes attributable to formulation representation choices.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absolute Residual Tests Are Not Representation Invariant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of nonsingular row transformations on absolute feasibility residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Ax=b\) and \(DAx=Db\) be equivalent systems, where \(D\) is nonsingular. For any candidate \(\widehat x\), define \(\widehat r=A\widehat x-b\) and \(\widehat r_D=DA\widehat x-Db\). Then
\[
\widehat r_D=D\widehat r,
\]
so \(\|\widehat r_D\|\leq\|D\|\,\|\widehat r\|\) and \(\|\widehat r\|\leq\|D^{-1}\|\,\|\widehat r_D\|\). Consequently, one fixed absolute residual tolerance can accept one representation and reject an exactly equivalent row-transformed representation. Any invariant comparison must account explicitly for the transformation or representation scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular row transformations preserve exact solutions but change absolute residuals, making fixed absolute feasibility tolerances representation dependent.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is nonsingular.
The same candidate point \(\widehat x\) is tested in both representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat r_D=D\widehat r\), so a fixed absolute residual threshold is not invariant under equivalent row transformations.

notation.meaning: Residuals in the original and transformed representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Residual Tests Are Not Representation Invariant

assumptions_latex: The parameter satisfies \(0<\varepsilon<1\).
The equation is evaluated under perturbations of its right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An exactly equivalent scaled representation can have condition number \(1/\varepsilon\) and amplify perturbations by the same order.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the diagonal family directly exhibits representation-dependent condition growth and perturbation amplification
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal family exhibiting instability under equivalent rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
A_\varepsilon x=b,\qquad A_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon),\qquad 0<\varepsilon<1.
\]
Multiplying the second equation by \(1/\varepsilon\) gives an exactly equivalent representation in exact arithmetic. Nevertheless,
\[
\kappa_2(A_\varepsilon)=\frac{1}{\varepsilon}.
\]
A perturbation \(\delta b=(0,\delta)\) changes the solution by \(\delta x=(0,\delta/\varepsilon)\). Hence equivalent feasible sets can have arbitrarily different numerical sensitivity as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\); exact reformulation equivalence alone does not ensure stable residual tests, basis computations, or recovered variable values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equivalent diagonal system with coefficient \(\varepsilon\) has condition number \(1/\varepsilon\), so small data errors can be greatly amplified.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Induced Instability

children.title: Scaling–Conditioning Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Cases where local rescaling changes the numerical behavior of the broader representation.

assumptions_latex: Candidate scalings use positive diagonal matrices \(D_r,D_c\).
Coefficient spread and spectral conditioning are evaluated on the scaled matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaling choices should be compared by both coefficient spread and condition number because neither criterion universally controls the other.

notation.meaning: Ratio of largest to smallest nonzero coefficient magnitude.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coefficient spread and singular-value conditioning are distinct representation metrics

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Preliminaries from linear algebra, matrix theory, and Euclidean geometry p. 4

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\), define the nonzero coefficient spread by
\[
\rho(\widehat A)=\frac{\max_{i,j:\widehat a_{ij}\ne0}|\widehat a_{ij}|}{\min_{i,j:\widehat a_{ij}\ne0}|\widehat a_{ij}|}.
\]
Coefficient scaling may decrease \(\rho(\widehat A)\) while increasing \(\kappa_2(\widehat A)\), or conversely, because entry magnitudes do not determine singular-value geometry. A scaling is therefore dominated when another admissible scaling weakly reduces both \(\rho\) and \(\kappa_2\), with at least one strict reduction. Nondominated choices express a scaling-conditioning tradeoff; exact feasibility equivalence does not select a unique numerical optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient range and spectral condition number are distinct scaling criteria; prefer nondominated scalings rather than assuming improvement in one improves the other.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling–Conditioning Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent semantics of a one-way native indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The native indicator constraint
\[
z=1\ \Longrightarrow\ a^{\mathsf T}x\le b,
\qquad z\in\{0,1\},
\]
has semantic feasible set
\[
S=\{(x,0):x\in X\}\cup\{(x,1):x\in X,\ a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\},
\]
where \(X\) contains the remaining domain restrictions. The implication imposes no converse: satisfaction of the inequality does not force \(z=1\). A native interface avoids requiring the modeler to supply a big-M coefficient, but its internal reformulation, continuous relaxation, and propagation strength are solver-dependent and are not determined by these semantics alone.

children.title: Native Logic Interfaces

knowledge_statements.title: Native Logic Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic definition of a solver-native logical constraint interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be binary variables and let \(A_j(x)\) be atomic predicates over decision variables \(x\). A native logic interface accepts a Boolean formula \(\varphi(B,A_1(x),\ldots,A_m(x))\) as one solver object. Its feasible set is \[F_\varphi=\{(x,B):\varphi(B,A_1(x),\ldots,A_m(x))=\mathrm{true}\}.\] The interface is semantically exact when the solver's internal reformulation \(R\), possibly using auxiliary variables \(u\), satisfies \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,B}(R)=F_\varphi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A native logic interface accepts a Boolean formula directly and is exact when its internal extended formulation projects to precisely the formula’s feasible assignments.
assumptions_latex: Each atomic predicate \(A_j(x)\) has a well-defined truth value on the declared domain.
Variables in \(B\) are binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,B}(R)=F_\varphi\).

notation.meaning: Feasible assignments satisfying the logical formula.
Solver-generated formulation in original and auxiliary variables.

children.title: Solver Reformulation Behavior
children.top_down_role: Internal transformation choices applied to native logical structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver Reformulation Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness criterion for internal reformulation of native logical constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\times\{0,1\}^p\) be the feasible set declared through native logical constraints. Suppose a solver replaces those constraints by \(R\subseteq X\times\{0,1\}^p\times U\). The reformulation preserves integer-feasible semantics exactly when \[\operatorname{proj}_{x,z}(R)=F.\] This equality does not imply equality of continuous relaxations: after relaxing integrality, \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,z}(R_{\mathrm{LP}})\) may strictly contain \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\), so reformulation choices can affect bounds and propagation without changing feasible integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver reformulation must preserve projected integer-feasible solutions, although different exact reformulations may have unequal continuous relaxations and propagation strength.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is the solver's internal extended formulation.
Projection eliminates only internally introduced variables \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact semantics require \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,z}(R)=F\), while generally \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,z}(R_{\mathrm{LP}})\neq\operatorname{conv}(F)\).

notation.meaning: Continuous relaxation of the internal reformulation.

review_flags: source needed for solver reformulation and relaxation behavior

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf, but the domains X and U and the construction of the continuous relaxation need clarification, and no cited source supports the reformulation and relaxation claims.

children.title: Propagation Preservation
children.top_down_role: Retention or loss of high-level inference strength after solver reformulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semantic Equivalence Does Not Ensure Propagation Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact feasible-set reformulation and equality of propagation fixpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when a reformulation \(R\) is semantically exact, \(\operatorname{proj}_x(R)=F\), soundness of its propagators alone does not imply \(\operatorname{proj}_x P_R(D\times D_u)=P_N(D)\). Propagation preservation is relative to the specified native and reformulated propagation operators, their scheduling to fixpoint, and the auxiliary-domain initialization. Either operator may yield a strictly smaller projected domain than the other without violating soundness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact feasible-set equivalence and sound propagation do not guarantee equal propagation strength; preservation must compare specified fixpoint operators and initialization conventions.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x(R)=F.
P_N\text{ and }P_R\text{ are sound domain contractors iterated under their stated conventions.}
D_u\text{ contains every auxiliary value compatible with }D.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x(R)=F\centernot\Longrightarrow \operatorname{proj}_xP_R(D\times D_u)=P_N(D).

notation.meaning: Native and reformulated propagation fixpoint operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Equivalence Does Not Ensure Propagation Preservation
Propagation Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-level criterion comparing native and reformulated propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every initial box domain \(D\) on original variables, let \(P_N(D)\) denote the fixpoint obtained by sound native-constraint propagation. Let \(P_R(D\times D_u)\) be the fixpoint for a reformulation with auxiliary domain \(D_u\). The reformulation preserves propagation on original variables precisely when \[\operatorname{proj}_{x}P_R(D\times D_u)=P_N(D)\quad\text{for every admissible }D,\] where \(D_u\) is initialized to contain every auxiliary value compatible with \(D\). Inclusion instead of equality characterizes one-sided dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation is preserved when reformulated propagation, projected onto original variables, produces exactly the same domain fixpoint as native propagation for every initial domain.
assumptions_latex: Both propagation operators are sound and are iterated to a fixpoint.
Auxiliary domains initially contain all values compatible with the original domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{x}P_R(D\times D_u)=P_N(D)\) for every admissible \(D\).
review_flags: exact propagation-equivalence convention needs a constraint-programming source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition matches the leaf, but propagation fixpoints and compatible auxiliary-domain initialization depend on a precise constraint-programming convention for which no source is supplied.

children.title: Native SOS Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing representation of special ordered set structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-defined native SOS1 and SOS2 declarations, including singleton handling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SOS1 declaration is well defined for \(k\geq1\). The adjacent-pair formulation of SOS2 requires \(k\geq2\) and a strict total order of its members, usually induced by distinct weights \(w_1<\cdots<w_k\). If \(k=1\), SOS2 must either be rejected or explicitly interpreted as allowing support contained in the singleton; the adjacent-pair formula with \(j\in\{1,\ldots,k-1\}\) does not cover that case. Tied ordering weights do not determine SOS2 adjacency without an additional tie-breaking order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOS2 adjacent-pair semantics require at least two distinctly ordered members; singleton SOS2 and tied weights require an explicit convention.
assumptions_latex: k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq1}.
\text{The solver interface uses member weights to define SOS2 order.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k\geq2\ \land\ w_1<\cdots<w_k\text{ suffices for the standard adjacent-pair SOS2 definition.}

notation.meaning: Ordering weight assigned to member i.

knowledge_statements.title: SOS Cardinality and Ordering Preconditions
Native SOS Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-native SOS1 and SOS2 declarations with explicit semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For indexed variables \((\lambda_i)_{i=1}^k\) with distinct ordering weights \(w_1<\cdots<w_k\), an SOS1 declaration imposes \[\bigl|\{i:\lambda_i\neq0\}\bigr|\leq1.\] An SOS2 declaration imposes \[\{i:\lambda_i\neq0\}\subseteq\{j,j+1\}\quad\text{for some }j\in\{1,\ldots,k-1\}.\] A native SOS interface submits the variables, SOS type, and ordering weights directly, leaving branching, propagation, and any internal reformulation to the solver while retaining these feasible-set semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A native SOS interface declares at most one nonzero variable for SOS1 or at most two adjacent nonzeros in the supplied order for SOS2.
assumptions_latex: The ordering weights satisfy \(w_1<\cdots<w_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: SOS1 permits at most one nonzero entry; SOS2 permits nonzero entries only within one adjacent index pair.

notation.meaning: Member variables of the special ordered set.

review_flags: authoritative SOS definition and native-interface source required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The SOS definitions fit the leaf, but an authoritative locator is absent. The SOS2 formula also requires k at least 2 or a separate convention for a singleton SOS2.

knowledge_statements.title: Native Piecewise Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous univariate piecewise-linear graph represented by an ordered native declaration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t_1<\cdots<t_k\) be breakpoints and let \(v_i=f(t_i)\). The graph of the continuous linear interpolant on \([t_1,t_k]\) is represented by \[x=\sum_{i=1}^k t_i\lambda_i,\qquad y=\sum_{i=1}^k v_i\lambda_i,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i=1,\qquad \lambda_i\geq0,\] together with the SOS2 condition that the positive \(\lambda_i\) occupy at most two adjacent indices. A native piecewise interface declares \((t_i,v_i)\) and the relation \(y=f(x)\) directly with these graph semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A native piecewise-linear interface declares ordered breakpoints and values; its graph equals the convex-combination formulation with adjacent-support weights.
assumptions_latex: Breakpoints satisfy \(t_1<\cdots<t_k\).
The represented function is the continuous linear interpolant through \((t_i,v_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The native relation \(y=f(x)\) equals the displayed adjacent-support convex-combination graph.
review_flags: piecewise-interface representation requires an authoritative source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The adjacent-support representation is standard and appropriate, but no authoritative source is cited for either the representation or the asserted native-interface graph semantics.

children.title: Specialized Handler Selection
children.top_down_role: Solver or formulation regimes governing the use of specialized native handlers.

knowledge_statements.title: Specialized Handler Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics-constrained selection among solver handlers for ordered structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be an ordered constraint and let \(\mathcal H(S)\) contain candidate native, extended-formulation, and generic handlers. A valid handler must satisfy \(\operatorname{proj}_x F(H,S)=F(S)\). Given an implementation-dependent predicted cost \(C(H,S)\), specialized handler selection chooses \[H^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{H\in\mathcal H(S)} C(H,S)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \operatorname{proj}_x F(H,S)=F(S).\] The cost may combine relaxation weakness, propagation work, formulation size, and expected branching effort, but semantic exactness is mandatory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a specialized handler by minimizing predicted computational cost among handlers whose projected feasible set exactly matches the ordered constraint.
assumptions_latex: Every candidate handler has a defined extended feasible set \(F(H,S)\).
The cost score \(C(H,S)\) is fixed before selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H^*\) minimizes \(C(H,S)\) over semantically exact handlers.

notation.meaning: Available handlers for ordered constraint S.
Predicted computational cost of handler H.

review_flags: cost functional is an abstract selection principle requiring solver-interface evidence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits handler selection, but the proposed cost-minimization model is an abstract implementation-dependent prescription without authoritative solver-interface evidence.

children.title: Ordered-Structure Preservation
children.top_down_role: Retention of ordering information through reformulation and presolve.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compressed Adjacency Can Destroy SOS2 Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for eliminating SOS2 members and compressing the surviving order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an SOS2 have ordered members \(1\prec2\prec3\), and suppose member \(2\) is fixed to zero and eliminated. Declaring the surviving members \(1\prec'3\) adjacent permits simultaneous nonzero values at \(1\) and \(3\), although \(\{1,3\}\) was not an allowed support originally. Therefore zero-fixed elimination must preserve the adjacency relation induced by the original order, rather than automatically treating consecutive survivors as adjacent. A fixed nonzero member additionally restricts all other possible nonzero members to its original neighbors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compressing the order after eliminating an interior SOS2 member can create a false adjacency; original adjacency, including restrictions caused by fixed nonzeros, must be retained.
assumptions_latex: \text{The original constraint has SOS2 support semantics.}
1\prec2\prec3.
\lambda_2=0\text{ is eliminated in the zero-fixed example.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{1,3\}\notin\mathcal S_{\mathrm{original}}\quad\text{but compressed adjacency would admit }\{1,3\}.

notation.meaning: Original family of feasible SOS2 supports.

review_flags: qualifies_seed_phrase: adjacency among surviving members must mean adjacency inherited from the original ordered support graph, not adjacency after order compression
knowledge_statements.title: Compressed Adjacency Can Destroy SOS2 Semantics
Ordered-Structure Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation criterion for ordered supports under reformulation or presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((V,\prec)\) be the ordered members of a native constraint, and let \((V',\prec')\) be its surviving or substituted representation. Ordered structure is preserved when there is an injective map \(\iota:V'\to V\) such that \[u\prec' v\iff \iota(u)\prec\iota(v),\] and every feasible support in the transformed constraint maps to a feasible support of the original constraint, with every original feasible support representable after eliminated fixed members are removed. For SOS2, this requires preservation of adjacency among surviving nonfixed members.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformation preserves ordered structure when it preserves relative order and maps transformed feasible supports exactly to the original supports after fixed-member elimination.
assumptions_latex: Eliminated members are fixed or represented by exact substitutions.
The original and transformed constraints have well-defined feasible-support families.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order embedding and feasible-support correspondence preserve the ordered constraint semantics.

notation.meaning: Embedding of transformed members into the original order.

review_flags: formal preservation criterion needs a presolve or ordered-constraint source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is locally relevant, but exact representability after fixed-member elimination and the treatment of SOS2 adjacency require a formal sourced convention.

children.title: Expression-Graph Lifting
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-variable generation from nonlinear expression structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Graph Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact auxiliary-variable lifting of a factorable expression DAG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a factorable expression \(f(x)\) be represented by a directed acyclic graph with leaves \(x_i\) and internal nodes \(v\). Introduce one variable \(y_v\) per internal node and impose \[y_v=\phi_v\bigl((y_u)_{u\in\operatorname{pred}(v)}\bigr)\] in topological order, interpreting leaf outputs as the corresponding \(x_i\). If \(r\) is the root, then the lifted graph \(L\) satisfies \[\operatorname{proj}_{x,y_r}(L)=\{(x,y_r):y_r=f(x)\}.\] Repeated subexpressions may share a single node and auxiliary variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expression-graph lifting introduces one auxiliary variable per operation node; projecting the resulting defining equations recovers the original expression graph exactly.
assumptions_latex: The expression is factorable into operations \(\phi_v\) with specified domains.
The expression graph is acyclic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,y_r}(L)=\{(x,y_r):y_r=f(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: Elementary operation at internal node v.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite explicit acyclic expression graph with internal-node set \(V_I\). Introducing one auxiliary variable and one defining relation for every \(v\in V_I\) uses \(|V_I|\) auxiliary variables and \(|V_I|\) relations. A topological ordering and these records can be constructed in \(O(|V|+|E|)\) time and storage, excluding the encoding cost of the elemental relations themselves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit expression DAG yields one auxiliary and one relation per internal node and can be lifted in linear administrative time and storage.

\text{Per-node and per-edge administrative data have constant size.}
\text{Elemental-relation encoding cost is excluded.}
