children.title: Dynamic Row Exposure
children.top_down_role: Incremental presentation of formulation constraints to the solver.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact meaning of a no-violation response from a declared row-family oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_0\supseteq F\), and let \(\mathcal C\) be inequalities valid for \(F\). If an exact oracle certifies that \(x^t\in R_0\) violates no inequality in \(\mathcal C\), then \(x^t\in R_0\cap\bigcap_{(a,b)\in\mathcal C}\{x:a^Tx\le b\}\). This certifies membership in \(F\) only if that intersection equals \(F\); if it equals only \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\), it certifies convex-hull membership rather than membership in a nonconvex \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A no-row response certifies membership only in the relaxation described by the complete searched family; target feasibility requires that this relaxation equal the target.
assumptions_latex: The oracle is complete over the declared family \(\mathcal C\).
Every inequality in \(\mathcal C\) is valid for \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^t\in R_0\cap\bigcap_{(a,b)\in\mathcal C}\{x:a^Tx\le b\}.

notation.meaning: Complete valid-row family searched by the oracle.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete-Separation Termination Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exposure-round bound for a finite declared row family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be a finite valid-row family. If every nonterminal exposure round adds at least one previously unexposed row from \(\mathcal C\), exposed rows are retained, and termination occurs when no unexposed member of \(\mathcal C\) is violated, then row exposure has at most \(|\mathcal C|\) nonterminal rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a finite row family, retained rows, and at least one new row per nonterminal round, exposure terminates after at most the number of available rows.
assumptions_latex: |\mathcal C|<\infty.
Each nonterminal round exposes at least one previously unexposed row.
Exposed rows are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{exposure}}\le |\mathcal C|.

notation.meaning: Finite declared family of valid rows.

review_flags: The bound counts exposure rounds, not reoptimizations or arithmetic operations.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Family Termination Bound
Dynamic Row Exposure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint generation through a valid-row separation oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial relaxation \(R_0\supseteq F\), a valid-row family \(\mathcal C\), and a separation oracle \(S\), solve \(R_t\) to obtain \(x^t\). If \(S(x^t)\) returns rows \(a_j^Tx\leq b_j\) that are valid for \(F\) and violated by \(x^t\), set \[R_{t+1}=R_t\cap\bigcap_j\{x:a_j^Tx\leq b_j\}.\] Otherwise stop and return \(x^t\). A finite implementation may also stop at prescribed resource limits and return the current relaxation and incumbent status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic row exposure repeatedly solves a relaxation, separates violated valid inequalities, adds them, and stops when none are found or a resource limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: Every row returned by \(S\) is valid for \(F\).
Each unrestricted iteration solves the current relaxation sufficiently to query \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every update preserves \(F\subseteq R_{t+1}\subseteq R_t\).
review_flags: authoritative cutting-plane or row-generation locator required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits dynamic row exposure and its monotonicity conclusion is sound, but no cutting-plane locator is supplied and stopping without rows is not a certificate unless the oracle's completeness is specified.

children.title: Dynamic Column Exposure
children.top_down_role: Incremental presentation of formulation variables to the solver.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Column Exposure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master column generation for a standard-form minimization linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) index the admissible columns of the full master linear program \[\min_{\lambda}\left\{\sum_{j\in J}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_j\lambda_j=b,\ \lambda_j\geq0\text{ for all }j\in J\right\}.\] Given a finite set \(J_0\subseteq J\), at iteration \(t\) solve the restricted master over \(J_t\) and obtain an optimal dual vector \(\pi^t\in\mathbb R^m\) for the equality constraints. An exact pricing oracle computes \[\rho^t=\inf_{j\in J}\left(c_j-(\pi^t)^\top a_j\right).\] If it returns a column \(j_t\in J\) with negative reduced cost, set \(J_{t+1}=J_t\cup\{j_t\}\) and reoptimize. If \(\rho^t\geq0\), stop; then the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a standard-form minimization master, dynamic column exposure repeatedly solves a restricted master and adds an admissible negative-reduced-cost column. If exact pricing finds no negative reduced cost, the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master linear program.
assumptions_latex: The full and restricted master linear programs are feasible and attain the optima used by the algorithm.
Pricing is exact over every admissible column in \(J\).
Strong linear-programming duality applies to the full and restricted masters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\rho^t\geq0\), the current restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master linear program.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative master variable associated with column j.
Optimal dual vector for the restricted master's equality constraints.
Minimum reduced cost over all admissible columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency requirements after the active row set changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the restricted master was solved on \((I_t,J_t)\) and new rows enlarge the active set to \(I_{t+1}\). Before pricing can certify the updated master, every admissible column must have coefficients defined for all rows in \(I_{t+1}\), and pricing must use a dual solution certified for the current restricted master on \((I_{t+1},J_t)\). The old vector \(\pi^t\), indexed only by \(I_t\), is not by itself such a certificate; it may be used only after a valid extension and current-master optimality have been separately established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After rows change, pricing needs complete new-row coefficients and a dual solution certified for the current master; the old dual vector alone is noncertifying.
assumptions_latex: I_t\subsetneq I_{t+1}.
Reduced costs include multipliers for every active master row.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi^t\text{ alone does not certify reduced costs for the master on }(I_{t+1},J_t).

notation.meaning: Dual vector obtained before the row-set change.

review_flags: Reoptimization is sufficient but not logically necessary if a current optimal dual certificate is obtained by another valid method.
knowledge_statements.title: Current-State Pricing and Coefficient-Completion Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-master LP optimality certificate for a synchronized, coefficient-complete restricted-master state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the full linear program \(\min\{c^T\lambda:A\lambda\ge b,\ \lambda\ge0\}\), with row family \(I\) and column family \(J\), and its dual \(\max\{b^T\pi:A^T\pi\le c,\ \pi\ge0\}\). Let \((\lambda^t,\pi^t)\) be an optimal primal-dual pair for the restricted master on \((I_t,J_t)\). If exact separation certifies that the zero-extended \(\lambda^t\) satisfies every row in \(I\), and exact pricing using the zero extension of \(\pi^t\) certifies nonnegative reduced cost for every column in \(J\), then the two zero extensions are feasible for the full primal and dual and have equal objective values. They are therefore optimal for the full master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronized restricted-master primal-dual optimum certifies full-master LP optimality when complete separation and complete pricing both succeed using coefficient-complete current data.
assumptions_latex: (\lambda^t,\pi^t)\text{ is optimal for the current restricted master on }(I_t,J_t).
The separation and pricing oracles are exact over \(I\) and \(J\).
Every column has a defined coefficient in every row.
The displayed minimization and dual sign conventions apply.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^T\lambda^t=b^T\pi^t=\operatorname{val}(\mathrm{LP}_{I,J}).

notation.meaning: Currently exposed row and column families.
Full declared row and column families.

review_flags: This certifies the full master LP, not a nonconvex integer master.
Any row or column update invalidates the certificate until a current optimal primal-dual state is re-established.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Row-and-Column Fixed-Point Certificate
Joint Exposure Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating coordination of row separation and column pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize exposed rows \(I_0\) and columns \(J_0\). At iteration \(t\), solve the restricted master on \((I_t,J_t)\), obtaining primal solution \(x^t\) and dual solution \(\pi^t\). Add all selected valid rows violated by \(x^t\), then price columns using dual multipliers for the updated row set and add selected columns of negative reduced cost. Repeat until separation returns no violated row and exact pricing returns no negative-reduced-cost column, or until a declared resource limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint coordination alternates valid-row separation and negative-reduced-cost pricing, reoptimizing until both oracles certify no improving exposure.
assumptions_latex: The separation oracle returns only globally valid rows.
The pricing oracle returns only admissible columns.
Restricted masters are solved consistently after each exposure round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At unrestricted termination, no oracle-detectable violated valid row or negative-reduced-cost column remains.
review_flags: joint row-and-column coordination requires a dedicated authoritative source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but rows are added before pricing while the stated dual solution belongs to the pre-update master. Reoptimization and acquisition of dual multipliers for the updated row set must be specified and sourced.

children.title: Separation Ownership Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Division between formulation interfaces and externally owned separation machinery.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation Ownership Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound ownership contract for solver and user separation components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be the admissible valid-row family and partition responsibility as \(\mathcal C=\mathcal C_S\cup\mathcal C_U\), for solver-owned and user-owned separation. A sound ownership boundary requires each component to emit only rows from its assigned family, every required family to have at least one owner, and duplicate rows to be identified before insertion. Formally, if \(E_S(x)\) and \(E_U(x)\) are emitted rows, then \[E_S(x)\subseteq\mathcal C_S,\qquad E_U(x)\subseteq\mathcal C_U,\qquad \mathcal C_S\cup\mathcal C_U=\mathcal C.\] Overlap is permitted only with deterministic duplicate suppression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separation boundary assigns each valid-row family to solver or user code, enforces sound emissions and coverage, and suppresses duplicates in overlapping ownership.
assumptions_latex: Every row family in \(\mathcal C\) is valid for the target feasible set.
Row equivalence is decidable by the insertion layer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Emitted rows are valid and assigned, all required families are owned, and overlapping emissions cannot create duplicate insertions.

notation.meaning: Rows emitted by solver and user separators.

review_flags: callback ownership and duplicate-management semantics need an authoritative interface source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ownership condition is implementation-specific and uncited. It also calls the assignment a partition while later permitting overlap; the intended cover-with-overlap semantics require clarification.

children.title: Pricing Ownership Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Division between formulation interfaces and externally owned pricing machinery.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Ownership Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact ownership condition for column generation in a minimization master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the master problem own the linking constraints, their dual vector \(\pi\), the active column set \(J_R\), and column acceptance. Let the pricing oracle own the admissible column family \(J\), column data \((a_j,c_j)\), and global minimization of reduced cost. The boundary is valid when the oracle either returns \(j^*\in J\) satisfying \(c_{j^*}-a_{j^*}^{\mathsf T}\pi<0\), or certifies \(\inf_{j\in J}(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi)\ge 0\); only the master may add the returned column to \(J_R\) or declare the current relaxation pricing-complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master controls dual information and column admission; the pricing oracle generates a negative-reduced-cost column or certifies that none exists.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is the complete admissible column family.
The pricing problem is solved globally and exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{j\in J}(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi)\ge 0\) certifies pricing completeness.

notation.meaning: columns currently exposed to the restricted master
dual vector for master linking constraints

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports solver-oracle ownership boundaries.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost condition is plausible and the condition kind fits the ownership-boundary leaf, but no inspectable source supports the asserted master–oracle responsibilities or completeness certificate.

children.title: Structure Preservation under Presolve
children.top_down_role: Interactions between automatic transformations and exploitable logical, conic, or decomposable structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Elimination Need Not Preserve Incidence Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of row-variable incidence preservation under an exact presolve elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{(x_1,x_2,z)\in\mathbb R^3:z=x_1,\ z=x_2\}\). Eliminating \(z\) gives \(F'=\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2:x_1=x_2\}\), and \(\rho(x_1,x_2)=(x_1,x_2,x_1)\) maps \(F'\) bijectively onto \(F\). In the original bipartite row-variable incidence graph, \(x_1\) and \(x_2\) occur in different rows linked through \(z\); after elimination, one row contains both variables. Thus exact reconstruction does not preserve the original incidence graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a linking variable can preserve the feasible set exactly while creating direct row incidence between variables that previously occurred in different rows.
assumptions_latex: Variables are continuous and unrestricted.
Structure is measured by the row-variable incidence graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho(F')=F\quad\text{but the original row-variable incidence graph is not preserved.}

notation.meaning: Presolved feasible set after eliminating z.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Elimination Need Not Preserve Incidence Structure
Structure Preservation under Presolve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of declared logical, conic, or block structure by an exact presolve transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\times Y\) be a formulation carrying a declared structure \(\mathcal S\), and let presolve produce \(F'\subseteq X'\times Y'\) with reconstruction map \(\rho:F'\to F\). Presolve preserves \(\mathcal S\) when \(\rho(F')=F\), objective values agree under reconstruction, and there is a structure map sending every retained logical group, cone, or decomposition block of \(\mathcal S\) to a corresponding object in \(F'\). Eliminated objects must be reconstructible without introducing dependencies between blocks that were disjoint in \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve preserves structure when it is exactly reconstructible, preserves objectives, and retains the declared logical, conic, or decomposition relationships without creating cross-block dependencies.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(F'\) use the same optimization sense.
\(\rho\) is defined on every feasible point of \(F'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(F')=F\) and the declared incidence structure is preserved.

notation.meaning: declared logical, conic, or block structure

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses structure-preserving presolve.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This bespoke definition requires a source. It also refers to agreement of objective values without introducing objective functions and leaves the required structure map insufficiently formalized.

children.title: Computational Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Ways that valid and theoretically strong formulations can perform poorly or produce unreliable models.

children.title: Ideal but Computationally Inferior Formulations
children.top_down_role: Exact formulations defeated by size, density, degeneracy, or poor search behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Ideal but Computationally Inferior Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates polyhedral ideality from computational superiority on a prescribed instance and resource metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be an integer-feasible set, and let \(Q\) and \(R\) be exact mixed-integer formulations whose integer-feasible projections onto the original variables are \(X\). Formulation \(Q\) is ideal when \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\mathrm{LP}})=\operatorname{conv}(X)\). Given an instance \(I\) and a fixed resource metric \(T\), the ideal formulation \(Q\) is computationally inferior to \(R\) on \(I\) when \(T(Q,I)>T(R,I)\). Ideality alone does not imply the reverse inequality because it constrains the projected relaxation but not formulation size, density, degeneracy, numerical behavior, or the work performed by a specified solution procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ideal formulation is computationally inferior on a prescribed instance when it consumes more of a fixed resource than another exact formulation. Ideality controls the projected relaxation and does not by itself guarantee lower computational work.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) and \(R\) are exact formulations of the same set \(X\).
The instance \(I\), resource metric \(T\), solver configuration, and comparison protocol are fixed before evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_{\mathrm{LP}})=\operatorname{conv}(X)\) does not imply \(T(Q,I)\le T(R,I)\).

notation.meaning: fixed computational resource metric for formulation Q on instance I

source_refs.locator: 1.7 Good and Ideal Formulations p. 15
5.1 Comparing the Strength of Different Formulations p. 70

review_flags: Computational inferiority is defined relative to a fixed instance and evaluation protocol.

source_witnesses.locator: 1.7 Good and Ideal Formulations p. 15
5.1 Comparing the Strength of Different Formulations p. 70

children.title: Compact but Weak Formulations
children.top_down_role: Small representations whose relaxations provide inadequate bounds or propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact but Weak Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial formulation size does not prevent a strict or asymptotically unbounded additive relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(n\), let \(X_n\) be an integer-feasible set with input encoding length \(\ell_n\), and let \(Q_n\) be an exact formulation of \(X_n\) having at most a polynomial number of variables and constraints in \(\ell_n\). For a minimization objective \(c_n\), define \(z_n^{\mathrm{IP}}=\min\{c_n^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X_n\}\) and \(z_n^{\mathrm{LP}}=\min\{c_n^{\mathsf T}x:(x,y)\in(Q_n)_{\mathrm{LP}}\}\). The formulation is weak for instance \(n\) and objective \(c_n\) when \(z_n^{\mathrm{LP}}<z_n^{\mathrm{IP}}\). The family has an unbounded additive relaxation gap when \(\sup_n\bigl(z_n^{\mathrm{IP}}-z_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\bigr)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formulation family can have polynomial size while still giving a strictly weak LP bound; its additive relaxation gap may even be unbounded across the family.
assumptions_latex: Each \(Q_n\) projects exactly to \(X_n\) at integer-feasible points.
Both \(z_n^{\mathrm{IP}}\) and \(z_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\) are finite for every evaluated \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_n^{\mathrm{LP}}<z_n^{\mathrm{IP}}\) witnesses relaxation weakness despite polynomial formulation size.

notation.meaning: input encoding length of instance n
compact exact formulation for instance n

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Comparing the Strength of Different Formulations p. 70
1.7 Good and Ideal Formulations p. 15

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Comparing the Strength of Different Formulations p. 70
1.7 Good and Ideal Formulations p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact Exact Family with Unbounded Multiplicative Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that polynomial encoding size does not imply a uniform multiplicative relaxation-gap bound, even when the additive gap stays bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each integer \(n\ge2\), consider \(Q_n=\{x\in\{0,1\}:nx\ge1\}\) with minimization objective \(x\). Its integer-feasible set is \(X_n=\{1\}\), while its continuous relaxation has optimum \(z_n^{\mathrm{LP}}=1/n\) and its integer optimum is \(z_n^{\mathrm{IP}}=1\). The formulation has one variable, one inequality, and encoding length \(O(\log n)\), but \(z_n^{\mathrm{IP}}/z_n^{\mathrm{LP}}=n\to\infty\), whereas \(z_n^{\mathrm{IP}}-z_n^{\mathrm{LP}}=1-1/n<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-variable exact binary formulation has logarithmic encoding length and an unbounded multiplicative LP gap, although its additive gap remains below one.
assumptions_latex: The multiplicative minimization gap uses positive finite LP and integer values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{size}(Q_n)=O(\log n)\), \(z_n^{\mathrm{IP}}/z_n^{\mathrm{LP}}=n\to\infty\), and \(z_n^{\mathrm{IP}}-z_n^{\mathrm{LP}}<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Compact Exact Family with Unbounded Multiplicative Gap

children.title: Numerically Unstable Liftings
children.top_down_role: Lifted formulations compromised by scaling, conditioning, or tolerance interactions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrarily Large Tolerance Amplification in an Exact Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact two-equation liftings with unbounded residual-to-projected-error amplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M>0\), let \[F_M=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x-My=0,\ y=0\}.\] Then \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_M)=\{0\}\). For every \(\delta>0\), the point \((M\delta,\delta)\) has maximum equation residual \(\delta\), whereas \(\operatorname{dist}(M\delta,\{0\})=M\delta\). Thus the residual-to-projected-error amplification is at least \(M\) and is unbounded over this family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact lifting can amplify an accepted equation residual by an arbitrarily large factor in the original variable.
assumptions_latex: Residual and distance use the absolute-value norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(M\delta,\operatorname{proj}_xF_M)/\delta=M\).
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrarily Large Tolerance Amplification in an Exact Lifting

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Raw Feasibility Tolerances Are Not Scaling Invariant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of positive row scaling on absolute feasibility tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{z:Az\le b,\ Cz=d\}\) and positive diagonal matrices \(S,T\), replacing the constraints by \(SAz\le Sb\) and \(TCz=Td\) leaves \(F\) unchanged. For a fixed absolute tolerance \(\tau>0\), however, define \[F_\tau(A,C)=\{z:\|(Az-b)_+\|_\infty\le\tau,\ \|Cz-d\|_\infty\le\tau\}.\] In general \(F_\tau(A,C)\ne F_\tau(SA,TC)\), so equivalent exact liftings can have different tolerance-induced projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row scaling preserves exact feasibility but can change the points accepted by an absolute feasibility tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(T\) are positive diagonal matrices.
The same absolute residual tolerance is applied after scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(A,C)=F(SA,TC)\), but generally \(F_\tau(A,C)\ne F_\tau(SA,TC)\).

notation.meaning: set accepted under the displayed absolute residual test

knowledge_statements.title: Raw Feasibility Tolerances Are Not Scaling Invariant

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hoffman Error Bound for Linear Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-to-distance conditioning for a nonempty linear lifted system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{z=(x,y):Az\le b,\ Cz=d\}\ne\varnothing\), and define \(\rho(z)=\|(Az-b)_+\|+\|Cz-d\|\). For fixed finite-dimensional norms, there exists \(H<\infty\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(z,F)\le H\rho(z)\quad\text{for every }z.\] If projection onto the \(x\)-coordinates is nonexpansive for the selected norms, then \[\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{proj}_xF)\le H\rho(z).\] Hence \(\rho(z)\le\tau\) guarantees projected error at most \(H\tau\); a large scaling-dependent constant makes the lifting tolerance-sensitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hoffman's error bound converts a linear lifted-system residual into an original-space distance bound, whose amplification factor may be large and scaling dependent.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonempty finite-dimensional polyhedron.
The residual and distance norms and the row scaling are fixed.
Coordinate projection is nonexpansive for the selected product and original-space norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{proj}_xF)\le H\rho(z)\).

notation.meaning: Hoffman error-bound constant for the scaled system and selected norms
combined equality and positive inequality residual

knowledge_statements.title: Hoffman Error Bound for Linear Liftings
Numerically Unstable Liftings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based instability of a lifted representation under finite feasibility tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{(x,y):g(x,y)=0,\ h(x,y)\le 0\}\) be an exact lifting of \(X=\operatorname{proj}_x(F)\). Define the constraint residual \(r(x,y)=\max\{\lVert g(x,y)\rVert,\lVert h(x,y)_+\rVert\}\). The lifting is numerically unstable near feasibility when there exists a sequence \((x_k,y_k)\) with \(r(x_k,y_k)\to0\) but \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X)/r(x_k,y_k)\to\infty\). Consequently, arbitrarily small accepted lifted residuals can correspond to disproportionately large violations in the represented original-variable set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifting is unstable when vanishing lifted-system residuals can hide disproportionately large original-space infeasibility, making feasibility tolerances unreliable.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and closed.
The selected norms and variable scaling are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(x_k,y_k)\to0\) need not imply a comparably scaled decrease of \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,X)\).

notation.meaning: maximum equality and positive inequality residual
represented feasible set in original variables

review_flags: No supplied locator establishes this residual-based numerical-stability criterion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits and the residual-ratio condition is mathematically coherent, but no source establishes it as the intended numerical-instability criterion for lifted formulations.

children.title: Auxiliary Symmetry Failure
children.top_down_role: Redundant lifted representations that create unnecessary search alternatives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates projection preservation from complete elimination of redundant auxiliary representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the same invariant action, projection preservation requires each nonempty fiber \(F_x\) to retain at least one feasible auxiliary point. In particular, if an orbit \(Gy\) is the entire fiber and \(S\cap Gy=\varnothing\), then \(x\notin\operatorname{proj}_x(F\cap(X\times S))\). Conversely, if \(|S\cap Gy|\ge2\) for a feasible orbit, at least two equivalent representatives remain. Thus orbit coverage is necessary for projection exactness in the single-orbit case, whereas one representative per orbit is necessary for complete symmetry removal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting the only orbit above an original point destroys exactness, while retaining multiple members of an orbit leaves symmetry unresolved.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is invariant under a group acting only on auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_x=Gy\land S\cap Gy=\varnothing\Rightarrow x\notin\operatorname{proj}_x(F\cap(X\times S))\), while \(|S\cap Gy|\ge2\) leaves redundant representatives.

notation.meaning: group orbit of auxiliary assignment y

knowledge_statements.title: Orbit-Coverage and Uniqueness Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes complete removal of auxiliary-orbit duplication while preserving the original projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\times Y\) be invariant under a finite group \(G\) acting trivially on \(X\), and let \(S\subseteq Y\). If every \(G\)-orbit in every nonempty fiber \(F_x=\{y:(x,y)\in F\}\) intersects \(S\) in exactly one point, then \(F^S=F\cap(X\times S)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F^S)=\operatorname{proj}_x(F)\) and retains exactly one representative of each feasible auxiliary orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting exactly one point from every feasible auxiliary orbit preserves all original solutions and removes orbit duplication.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and preserves \(F\).
\(G\) acts trivially on the original coordinates.
Every feasible auxiliary orbit intersects \(S\) exactly once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F^S)=\operatorname{proj}_x(F)\), with one retained representative per feasible \(G\)-orbit.

notation.meaning: auxiliary fiber over original point x

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Auxiliary Symmetry Breaking

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts symmetry-equivalent auxiliary representations above a fixed original solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) preserve a lifted feasible set \(F\subseteq X\times Y\) while acting trivially on \(X\). For \((x,y)\in F\), let \(G_y=\{g\in G:gy=y\}\). Every member of \(Gy\) is feasible above the same \(x\), and \[|Gy|=\frac{|G|}{|G_y|}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The orbit–stabilizer formula counts the auxiliary assignments generated from one feasible lifted representative.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite.
\((x,y)\in F\Rightarrow(x,gy)\in F\) for every \(g\in G\).
\(G\) acts trivially on the original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Orbit–Stabilizer Count of Auxiliary Duplicates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-preserving symmetry breaking for an interchangeable-pair lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F_k\), impose \(u_i\ge v_i\) for every \(i\). Together with \(u_i+v_i=1\) and binary variables, these inequalities force \((u_i,v_i)=(1,0)\). The restricted formulation retains one feasible lift, projects to \(X=\{1\}\), and eliminates every swap-equivalent alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordering each interchangeable binary pair selects one auxiliary representative without changing the original projection.
assumptions_latex: The symmetry group independently swaps each pair \((u_i,v_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x\!\left(F_k\cap\{u_i\ge v_i\ \forall i\}\right)=\{1\},\qquad \left|F_k\cap\{u_i\ge v_i\ \forall i\}\right|=1.

notation.meaning: canonical ordering constraint for auxiliary pair i

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Canonical-Representative Symmetry Breaking

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A lifted family whose auxiliary-branching leaves all project to one original solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\ge1\), let \(X=\{1\}\) and \[F_k=\{(x,u,v):x=1,\ u_i+v_i=1,\ u_i,v_i\in\{0,1\}\ (i=1,\ldots,k)\}.\] With a constant objective, its projection is \(X\), but it has \(2^k\) auxiliary assignments, permuted transitively by independently swapping each \(u_i\) and \(v_i\). A complete branching tree that successively fixes \(u_1,\ldots,u_k\) has \(2^k\) feasible leaves, all projecting to \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent interchangeable auxiliary pairs create exponentially many feasible search leaves representing the same original solution.
assumptions_latex: \(k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
The objective is constant and hence invariant under the pair swaps.
Branching successively fixes every \(u_i\) without symmetry breaking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |F_k|=2^k,\qquad \operatorname{proj}_x(F_k)=\{1\},\qquad L_k=2^k.

notation.meaning: binary lifted feasible set with k interchangeable auxiliary pairs
leaf count in the specified exhaustive auxiliary-branching tree

review_flags: The exponential count concerns the specified branching order, not every solver policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Exponential Auxiliary-Orbit Search Duplication
Auxiliary Symmetry Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundant symmetry acting only on lifted variables creates equivalent search alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\times Y\) be an exact lifted formulation and let a nontrivial finite group \(G\) act on \(Y\). Auxiliary symmetry is present when \((x,y)\in F\) implies \((x,gy)\in F\) for every \(g\in G\), the objective is invariant under this action, and some feasible orbit \(\{gy:g\in G\}\) has more than one element. It becomes a search failure mechanism when branching or enumeration distinguishes orbit members although they project to the same original solution \(x\), thereby creating redundant equivalent subproblems unless symmetry is broken or quotiented out.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted model has auxiliary symmetry when multiple transformed auxiliary assignments represent the same original solution and can generate redundant search subproblems.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) acts trivially on the original variables \(X\).
The group action preserves feasibility and objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\{gy:g\in G\}|>1\) yields equivalent auxiliary representations of the same \(x\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports auxiliary-variable symmetry as a search failure mechanism.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The group-action description correctly captures auxiliary symmetry and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the claimed search-failure mechanism lacks an inspectable supporting source.

children.title: Benchmark-Objective Generalization Failure
children.top_down_role: Formulation choices appearing strong only for narrow objectives, data regimes, or solver configurations.

children.title: Benchmark Overfitting
children.top_down_role: Formulation choices whose apparent quality depends on a narrow benchmark collection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure of formulation selection to generalize from a training benchmark to a disjoint held-out benchmark.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a fixed candidate class, let \(B_{\mathrm{train}}\cap B_{\mathrm{test}}=\varnothing\), and let \(\overline L_B(F)\) be a predeclared aggregate of a common run loss over benchmark \(B\). Select \(\widehat F\in\arg\min_{F\in\mathcal F}\overline L_{B_{\mathrm{train}}}(F)\) using a fixed tie rule. Benchmark overfitting at tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) is witnessed when \(\overline L_{B_{\mathrm{test}}}(\widehat F)-\min_{F\in\mathcal F}\overline L_{B_{\mathrm{test}}}(F)>\varepsilon\), with solver configuration, resource limits, aggregation, and failure penalties held fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A training-benchmark winner is benchmark-overfit when it is materially worse than the best candidate on a disjoint held-out benchmark under the same evaluation protocol.
assumptions_latex: \(B_{\mathrm{train}}\cap B_{\mathrm{test}}=\varnothing\).
The candidate class, selection rule, loss, aggregation, resource limits, failure penalties, and solver configuration are fixed before held-out evaluation.
Every required run has a defined loss, including censored or failed runs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline L_{B_{\mathrm{test}}}(\widehat F)-\min_{F\in\mathcal F}\overline L_{B_{\mathrm{test}}}(F)>\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: predeclared aggregate loss of formulation F on benchmark B
formulation selected on the training benchmark

review_flags: This is an operational evaluation definition, not a statistical generalization theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Benchmark Overfitting

children.title: Objective Overfitting
children.top_down_role: Formulation choices tailored to a narrow family of objective functions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a formulation choice selected on training objectives to generalize to disjoint held-out objectives on fixed feasible instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix feasible instances \(\mathcal I\), a candidate class \(\mathcal F\) of exact formulations of those instances, and a loss \(L(F,I,c)\). For disjoint objective sets \(C_{\mathrm{train}}\) and \(C_{\mathrm{test}}\), select \(\widehat F\) by minimizing a predeclared aggregate loss over \(\mathcal I\times C_{\mathrm{train}}\), with a fixed tie rule. It is objective-overfit at tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) when its aggregate loss over \(\mathcal I\times C_{\mathrm{test}}\) exceeds the best candidate aggregate loss there by more than \(\varepsilon\), while instances, solver configuration, resources, aggregation, and failure penalties remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formulation choice is objective-overfit when training-objective performance selects it, but it has material regret on disjoint held-out objectives for the same feasible instances.
assumptions_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{train}}\cap C_{\mathrm{test}}=\varnothing\).
Every candidate is exact for the fixed feasible instances.
The selection rule and all non-objective evaluation conditions are fixed before held-out evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline L_{C_{\mathrm{test}}}(\widehat F)-\min_{F\in\mathcal F}\overline L_{C_{\mathrm{test}}}(F)>\varepsilon\).
review_flags: Opposite rankings under two objectives alone do not establish overfitting; a training-based selection and held-out regret are required.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Overfitting

children.title: Data-Regime Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Loss of formulation performance when instance distributions or parameter ranges change.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute performance change or formulation-ranking reversal attributable to a change in the instance-data regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathfrak D\) be a prescribed family of instance distributions and let \(L(F,D)=\mathbb E_{I\sim D}[\ell(F,I)]\) be finite under a fixed evaluation protocol. Formulation \(F\) has absolute data-regime sensitivity at level \(\delta>0\) if \(|L(F,D_1)-L(F,D_2)|>\delta\) for some \(D_1,D_2\in\mathfrak D\). Pairwise formulation ranking is data-regime sensitive if formulations \(F_1,F_2\) and regimes \(D_1,D_2\) satisfy \(L(F_1,D_1)<L(F_2,D_1)\) and \(L(F_1,D_2)>L(F_2,D_2)\). Objectives, solver configuration, resources, aggregation, and failure treatment must remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Data-regime sensitivity is witnessed by a material loss change or a formulation-ranking reversal when only the instance distribution changes.
assumptions_latex: The relevant expected losses are finite.
All non-data evaluation factors are fixed across regimes.
The distributions belong to a predeclared admissible family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|L(F,D_1)-L(F,D_2)|>\delta\) or an opposite strict ordering of \(F_1,F_2\) across \(D_1,D_2\) witnesses data-regime sensitivity.

notation.meaning: run loss for formulation F on instance I

review_flags: Observed sample averages require separate statistical uncertainty control before being treated as expected-loss witnesses.
knowledge_statements.title: Data-Regime Sensitivity

children.title: Solver-Configuration Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Loss of apparent formulation quality under different solver settings or implementations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute performance change or formulation-ranking reversal attributable to solver configuration under a controlled protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a fixed instance benchmark, \(\Theta\) a prescribed set of solver configurations, and \(\overline L_B(F;\theta)\) a predeclared aggregate run loss. Formulation \(F\) has absolute configuration sensitivity at level \(\delta>0\) if \(|\overline L_B(F;\theta_1)-\overline L_B(F;\theta_2)|>\delta\) for some \(\theta_1,\theta_2\in\Theta\). Pairwise formulation ranking is configuration-sensitive if \(\overline L_B(F_1;\theta_1)<\overline L_B(F_2;\theta_1)\) and \(\overline L_B(F_1;\theta_2)>\overline L_B(F_2;\theta_2)\). Instances, objectives, hardware allocation, resource limits, aggregation, failure penalties, and randomness protocol must be controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solver-configuration sensitivity is witnessed by a material loss change or a formulation-ranking reversal when only the solver configuration changes.
assumptions_latex: The benchmark, objectives, hardware allocation, resource limits, and loss aggregation are fixed.
Solver versions, configurations, and randomness controls are recorded.
Failed and censored runs receive the same predeclared treatment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\overline L_B(F;\theta_1)-\overline L_B(F;\theta_2)|>\delta\text{ or an opposite strict ordering across }\theta_1,\theta_2\text{ witnesses sensitivity}.

notation.meaning: aggregate loss on fixed benchmark B under configuration theta

review_flags: The record repairs the seed's instance-level versus aggregate-loss notation mismatch.
knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Configuration Sensitivity

children.title: Cross-Regime Robustness
children.top_down_role: Stability of formulation quality across objectives, datasets, and solver configurations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes exact finite-regime verification from unsupported extrapolation beyond evaluated regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathcal R\) is finite and every \(L(G,r)\) is certified for \(G\in\mathcal F\) and \(r\in\mathcal R\), then \(\max_{r\in\mathcal R}R(F,r)\le\varepsilon\) certifies cross-regime robustness at level \(\varepsilon\). For an infinite \(\mathcal R\), verification on a finite sampled subset is not such a certificate unless a valid uniform upper bound on \(R(F,r)\) over the unevaluated regimes is also supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact maximum regret certifies robustness over a finite regime set; sampled checks alone do not certify an infinite regime family.
assumptions_latex: All losses and regime-wise baselines used in the finite maximum are certified.
For infinite regime families, any extrapolation uses a valid uniform upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\mathcal R|<\infty\Rightarrow\left(\max_{r\in\mathcal R}R(F,r)\le\varepsilon\right)\text{ is a certificate};\quad \mathcal R_0\subsetneq\mathcal R\text{ alone is insufficient}.

notation.meaning: finite evaluated subset of a larger regime family

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Regime Robustness Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly bounded formulation regret over a prescribed family of comparable evaluation regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) be fixed independently of the evaluated formulation, let \(\mathcal F\) be a fixed candidate class, and let \(L(F,r)\in\mathbb R\) be a comparable loss for formulation \(F\) in regime \(r\). Define additive regret \(R(F,r)=L(F,r)-\inf_{G\in\mathcal F}L(G,r)\). Formulation \(F\) is cross-regime robust at level \(\varepsilon\ge0\) when \(\sup_{r\in\mathcal R}R(F,r)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formulation is cross-regime robust when its worst loss above the regime-best candidate is uniformly bounded over a predeclared regime family.
assumptions_latex: The regime family and candidate class are fixed before evaluation.
Losses use a common scale and common treatment of resource limits, randomness, failures, and censoring.
\(\inf_{G\in\mathcal F}L(G,r)\) is finite for every \(r\in\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{r\in\mathcal R}\left[L(F,r)-\inf_{G\in\mathcal F}L(G,r)\right]\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: comparable loss of formulation F in regime r
additive regret relative to the best candidate in regime r

review_flags: Additive regret is used to avoid the positivity requirement of normalized regret.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Regime Robustness
